and holding them upward and facing forward, [that is] indeed for the ninth seed-syllable. / Then, turning the left hand upward, one should slowly bend half of it.
[Footnote mark]
1. The reading in the two manuscripts marked kha and ṅa is 'sarvasiddhyai'.
2. The reading in the manuscript marked kha is 'vairājaṃ nāgasaṃyutam'; the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'yauvījaṃ cāṅgasaṃyutam'.
3. The reading in the manuscript marked kha is 'yaḥ savyerdhe prakīrtitaḥ'. / [Page 70]

26.s:
varāhasya smṛtā mudrā aṅganāñca kramādimāḥ /
ekaikāṃ mocayedbaddhvā vāmamuṣṭo tathāgulīṃ //
26.d:
वराहस्य स्मृता मुद्रा अङ्गनाञ्च क्रमादिमाः /
एकैकां मोचयेद्बद्ध्वा वाममुष्टो तथागुलीं //
26.m: This is remembered as the ritual gesture of Varāha, and these are successively [those] of the ancillary [deities]: / having formed a left fist, one should release each single finger in turn.

26.s:
ākuñcayet pūrvamudrāṃ dakṣiṇepyevameva ca /
ūrdhvāṅguṣṭho vāmamuṣṭhirmudrāsiddhistato bhavet //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye mudrāpradarśanaṃ nāma
ṣaḍviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha saptaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
dīkṣāvidhikathanaṃ
26.d:
आकुञ्चयेत् पूर्वमुद्रां दक्षिणेप्येवमेव च /
ऊर्ध्वाङ्गुष्ठो वाममुष्ठिर्मुद्रासिद्धिस्ततो भवेत् //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये मुद्राप्रदर्शनं नाम
षड्विंशो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ सप्तविंशो ऽध्यायः
दीक्षाविधिकथनं
26.m:
One should contract the previous gesture, and similarly with the right [hand] as well: / the left fist with the thumb upright—thence comes success with the ritual gestures.
Thus in the glorious Agni Mahāpurāṇa, the twenty-sixth chapter, entitled 'Explanation of Ritual Gestures'.
Now, the twenty-seventh chapter.
Explanation of the Rules of Initiation

27.s:
nārada uvāca
vakṣye dīkṣāṃ sarvadāñca maṇḍalebje hariṃ yajet /
daśamyāmupasaṃhṛtya yāgadravyaṃ samastakaṃ //
27.d:
नारद उवाच
वक्ष्ये दीक्षां सर्वदाञ्च मण्डलेब्जे हरिं यजेत् /
दशम्यामुपसंहृत्य यागद्रव्यं समस्तकं //
27.m: Nārada said: / I shall explain initiation, which bestows everything. One should worship Hari in the lotus of the maṇḍala. / Having collected all the ritual sacrificial materials on the tenth lunar day,

27.s:
vinyasya nārasiṃhena sammantrya śatavārakaṃ /
sarṣapāṃstu phaḍantena(1) rakṣoghnān sarvataḥ kṣipet //
27.d:
विन्यस्य नारसिंहेन सम्मन्त्र्य शतवारकं /
सर्षपांस्तु फडन्तेन(1) रक्षोघ्नान् सर्वतः क्षिपेत् //
27.m: depositing [them] and consecrating them a hundred times with the Nārasiṃha mantra, / one should scatter mustard seeds that destroy demons in all directions with the mantra ending in phaṭ.

27.s:
śaktiṃ sarvātmakāṃ tatra nyaset prāsādarūpiṇīṃ /
sarvauṣadhiṃ samāhṛtya vikirānabhimantrayet //
27.d:
शक्तिं सर्वात्मकां तत्र न्यसेत् प्रासादरूपिणीं /
सर्वौषधिं समाहृत्य विकिरानभिमन्त्रयेत् //
27.m: There one should deposit the all-pervading energy embodied as the temple. / Having gathered all medicinal herbs, one should consecrate the scattering grains (vikira)

27.s:
śatavāraṃ śubhe pātre vāsudevena sādhakaḥ /
saṃsādhya paṇjagavyantu pañcabhirmūlamūrtibhiḥ //
27.d:
शतवारं शुभे पात्रे वासुदेवेन साधकः /
संसाध्य पण्जगव्यन्तु पञ्चभिर्मूलमूर्तिभिः //
27.m: a hundred times in an auspicious vessel with [the mantra of] Vāsudeva. The practitioner, / having prepared the five products of the cow with the five primary icons,

27.s:
nārāyaṇāntaiḥ samprokṣya kuśāgraistena tāṃbhuvaṃ(3)/
vikirānvāsudevena kṣipeduttānapāṇinā //
27.d:
नारायणान्तैः सम्प्रोक्ष्य कुशाग्रैस्तेन तांभुवं(3)/
विकिरान्वासुदेवेन क्षिपेदुत्तानपाणिना //
27.m: and having sprinkled that ground with the tips of kuśa grass [using the mantras] ending with Nārāyaṇa, / should scatter the grains with [the mantra of] Vāsudeva with the palm turned upward.

27.s:
tridhā pūrvamukhastiṣṭhan dhyāyet viṣṇuṃ tathā hṛdi /
vardhanyā sahite kumbhe sāṅgaṃ viṣṇuṃ prapūjayet //
:n
1 sarṣapāṃstadvadastreṇa iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 kuśāgreṇaiva tāṃ bhuvamiti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭḥaḥ
:p 71
27.d:
त्रिधा पूर्वमुखस्तिष्ठन् ध्यायेत् विष्णुं तथा हृदि /
वर्धन्या सहिते कुम्भे साङ्गं विष्णुं प्रपूजयेत् //
:न्
1 सर्षपांस्तद्वदस्त्रेण इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 कुशाग्रेणैव तां भुवमिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाट्ःअः
:प् 71
27.m:
Standing facing east, he should meditate three times on Viṣṇu in his heart. / In the pitcher accompanied by the vardhanī vessel, he should worship Viṣṇu together with his limbs.
[Footnote mark]
1. The reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'sarṣapāṃstadvadastreṇa'.
2. The reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'kuśāgreṇaiva tāṃ bhuvam'. / [Page 71]

27.s:
śatavāraṃ mantrayitvā tvastreṇaiva ca vardhanīṃ /
acchinnadhārayā siñcan īśānāntaṃ nayecca taṃ //
27.d:
शतवारं मन्त्रयित्वा त्वस्त्रेणैव च वर्धनीं /
अच्छिन्नधारया सिञ्चन् ईशानान्तं नयेच्च तं //
27.m: Having consecrated the vardhanī vessel a hundred times with the weapon-mantra (astra), / and sprinkling with an unbroken stream, one should carry it as far as the north-east.

27.s:
kalasaṃ pṛṣṭhato nītvā sthāpayedvikiropari /
saṃhṛtya vikirān darbhaiḥ kumbheśaṃ karkarīṃ yajet //
27.d:
कलसं पृष्ठतो नीत्वा स्थापयेद्विकिरोपरि /
संहृत्य विकिरान् दर्भैः कुम्भेशं कर्करीं यजेत् //
27.m: Bringing the pitcher from behind, one should place it upon the scattered grains; / gathering up the grains with darbha grass, one should worship the Lord of the pitcher and the water-jar (karkarī).

27.s:
savastraṃ pañcaratnāḍhyaṃ khaṇḍile pūjayeddhariṃ /
agnāvapi samabhyarcya mantrān sañjapya pūrvavat //
27.d:
सवस्त्रं पञ्चरत्नाढ्यं खण्डिले पूजयेद्धरिं /
अग्नावपि समभ्यर्च्य मन्त्रान् सञ्जप्य पूर्ववत् //
27.m: One should worship Hari clothed in garments and rich in the five gems on an altar; / having worshipped him in the fire as well, and reciting the mantras as before,

27.s:
prakṣālya puṇḍarīkena vilipyāntaḥ sugandhinā /
ukhāmājyena(1) saṃpūrya gokṣīreṇa tu sādhakaḥ //
27.d:
प्रक्षाल्य पुण्डरीकेन विलिप्यान्तः सुगन्धिना /
उखामाज्येन(1) संपूर्य गोक्षीरेण तु साधकः //
27.m: cleansing [the vessel] with a lotus and smearing the interior with fragrant substance, / the practitioner, filling the cooking-pot with clarified butter and cow's milk,

27.s:
ālokya vāsudevena(2) tataḥ saṅkarṣaṇena ca /
taṇḍulānājyasaṃsṛṣṭān kṣipet kṣīre susaṃskṛte //
27.d:
आलोक्य वासुदेवेन(2) ततः सङ्कर्षणेन च /
तण्डुलानाज्यसंसृष्टान् क्षिपेत् क्षीरे सुसंस्कृते //
27.m: inspecting [it] with [the mantra of] Vāsudeva and then with Saṅkarṣaṇa, / should throw rice grains mixed with clarified butter into the well-prepared milk.

27.s:
pradyumnena smāloḍya darvyā saṅghaṭṭayecchanaiḥ /
pakvamuttārayet paścādaniruddhena deśikaḥ //
27.d:
प्रद्युम्नेन स्मालोड्य दर्व्या सङ्घट्टयेच्छनैः /
पक्वमुत्तारयेत् पश्चादनिरुद्धेन देशिकः //
27.m: Having stirred it with Pradyumna, he should gently blend it with a ladle; / when cooked, the master (deśika) should afterwards take it off [the fire] with Aniruddha.

27.s:
prakṣālyālipya tat kuryādūrdhvapuṇḍraṃ tu bhasmanā /
nārāyaṇena pārśveṣu carumevaṃ susaṃskṛtaṃ //
27.d:
प्रक्षाल्यालिप्य तत् कुर्यादूर्ध्वपुण्ड्रं तु भस्मना /
नारायणेन पार्श्वेषु चरुमेवं सुसंस्कृतं //
27.m: Having washed and anointed it, he should make an upright mark (ūrdhvapuṇḍra) with ashes / on its sides with [the mantra of] Nārāyaṇa; [such is] the well-prepared sacred porridge (caru).

27.s:
bhāgamekaṃ tu devāya kalaśāya dvitīyakaṃ /
tṛtīyena tu bhāgena pradadyādāhutitrayaṃ //
27.d:
भागमेकं तु देवाय कलशाय द्वितीयकं /
तृतीयेन तु भागेन प्रदद्यादाहुतित्रयं //
27.m: [He should offer] one portion to the deity and a second to the pitcher; / with the third portion, he should make three oblations.

27.s:
śiṣyaiḥ saha caturthaṃ tu gururadyādviśuddhaye(3) /
nārāyaṇena sammantrya saptadhā kṣīravṛkṣajam //
27.d:
शिष्यैः सह चतुर्थं तु गुरुरद्याद्विशुद्धये(3) /
नारायणेन सम्मन्त्र्य सप्तधा क्षीरवृक्षजम् //
27.m: Together with the disciples, the guru should eat the fourth [portion] for purification. / Having consecrated seven times with Nārāyaṇa a tooth-stick

27.s:
dantakāṣṭhaṃ bhakṣayitvā tyaktvā jñātvāsvapātakaṃ /
aindrāgnyuttarakeśānīmukhaṃ patitamuttamaṃ //
27.d:
दन्तकाष्ठं भक्षयित्वा त्यक्त्वा ज्ञात्वास्वपातकं /
ऐन्द्राग्न्युत्तरकेशानीमुखं पतितमुत्तमं //
27.m: produced from a milky tree, chewing it and discarding it, he may discern good or bad fortune: / if it falls facing the east, south-east, north, or north-east, it is excellent;

27.s:
śubhaṃ siṃhaśataṃ hutvā(4) ācamyātha praviśya ca /
:n
1 utthāyājyeneti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 āloḍya vāsudevena iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 vivṛddhaye iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
4 śubhaṃ siddhamiti jñātvā ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 72
pūjāgāraṃ nyasenmantrī prācyāṃ viṣṇuṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ //
27.d:
शुभं सिंहशतं हुत्वा(4) आचम्याथ प्रविश्य च /
:न्
1 उत्थायाज्येनेति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 आलोड्य वासुदेवेन इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 विवृद्धये इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
4 शुभं सिद्धमिति ज्ञात्वा ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 72
पूजागारं न्यसेन्मन्त्री प्राच्यां विष्णुं प्रदक्षिणं //
27.m:
knowing it to be auspicious, having offered a hundred oblations to the Lion [Nṛsiṃha], sipping water, and then entering,
[Footnote mark]
1. The reading in the manuscript marked kha is 'utthāyājyena'.
2. The reading in the manuscript marked kha is 'āloḍya vāsudevena'.
3. The reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'vivṛddhaye'.
4. The reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'śubhaṃ siddhamiti jñātvā'. / [Page 72]
the mantra-practitioner should deposit Viṣṇu in the east of the worship-chamber, moving clockwise.

27.s:
saṃsārārṇavamagnānāṃ paśūnāṃ pāśamuktaye /
tvameva śaraṇaṃ deva sadā tvaṃ bhaktavatsala //
27.d:
संसारार्णवमग्नानां पशूनां पाशमुक्तये /
त्वमेव शरणं देव सदा त्वं भक्तवत्सल //
27.m: "For the liberation from bonds of the bound souls (paśu) sunk in the ocean of worldly existence, / you alone are the refuge, O Lord! You are always compassionate to devotees!

27.s:
devadevānujānīhi prākṛtaiḥ pāśabandhanaiḥ /
pāśitānmocayiṣyāmi tvatprasādāt paśūnimān //
27.d:
देवदेवानुजानीहि प्राकृतैः पाशबन्धनैः /
पाशितान्मोचयिष्यामि त्वत्प्रसादात् पशूनिमान् //
27.m: O God of gods, permit [me]: by your grace, I shall release / these bound souls who are bound by material bonds!"

27.s:
iti vijñāpya deveśaṃ sampraviśya paśūṃstataḥ /
dhāraṇābhistu saṃśodhya pūrvajjvalanādinā //
27.d:
इति विज्ञाप्य देवेशं सम्प्रविश्य पशूंस्ततः /
धारणाभिस्तु संशोध्य पूर्वज्ज्वलनादिना //
27.m: Having thus petitioned the Lord of gods, he enters, and then, / purifying the bound souls through meditative retentions (dhāraṇā) starting with fire as before,

27.s:
saṃskṛtya mūrtyā saṃyojya(1) netre baddhvā pradarśayet /
puṣpapūrṇāñjalīṃstatra kṣipettannāma yojayet //
27.d:
संस्कृत्य मूर्त्या संयोज्य(1) नेत्रे बद्ध्वा प्रदर्शयेत् /
पुष्पपूर्णाञ्जलींस्तत्र क्षिपेत्तन्नाम योजयेत् //
27.m: consecrating them, joining them with the icon, and blindfolding their eyes, he should present them; / they should cast folded hands full of flowers there, and he should assign their name.

27.s:
amantramarcanaṃ tatra pūrvavat kārayet kramāt /
yasyāṃ mūrtau patet puṣpaṃ tasya tannāma nirdiśet //
27.d:
अमन्त्रमर्चनं तत्र पूर्ववत् कारयेत् क्रमात् /
यस्यां मूर्तौ पतेत् पुष्पं तस्य तन्नाम निर्दिशेत् //
27.m: He should perform the worship there in order without mantras as before; / on whichever icon a flower falls, he should assign its name to him.

27.s:
śikhāntasammitaṃ sūtraṃ pādāṅguṣṭhādi ṣaḍguṇaṃ /
kanyāsu kartitaṃ raktaṃ(2) punastattriguṇīkṛtam //
27.d:
शिखान्तसम्मितं सूत्रं पादाङ्गुष्ठादि षड्गुणं /
कन्यासु कर्तितं रक्तं(2) पुनस्तत्त्रिगुणीकृतम् //
27.m: A cord measured from the big toe of the foot to the crest, six-fold, / spun by unmarried maidens, red, and then tripled again—

27.s:
yasyāṃ saṃlīyate viśvaṃ yato viśvaṃ prasūyate /
prakṛtiṃ prakriyābhedaiḥ saṃsthitāṃ tatra cintayet //
27.d:
यस्यां संलीयते विश्वं यतो विश्वं प्रसूयते /
प्रकृतिं प्रक्रियाभेदैः संस्थितां तत्र चिन्तयेत् //
27.m: in which the universe is dissolved, and from which the universe is brought forth, / in that [cord] one should meditate upon Primordial Nature (prakṛti) abiding through the different cosmic processes.

27.s:
tena prākṛtikān pāśān grathitvā tattvasaṅkhyayā(3) /
kṛtvā śarāve tat sūtraṃ kuṇḍapārśve nidhāya tu(4) //
27.d:
तेन प्राकृतिकान् पाशान् ग्रथित्वा तत्त्वसङ्ख्यया(3) /
कृत्वा शरावे तत् सूत्रं कुण्डपार्श्वे निधाय तु(4) //
27.m: Having tied the material bonds with that [cord] according to the number of cosmic principles (tattva), / placing that cord in a shallow dish, and depositing it beside the fire-pit,

27.s:
tatastattvāni sarvāṇi dhyātvā śiṣyatanau nyaset /
sṛṣṭikramāt prakṛtyādipṛthivyantāni deśikaḥ //
27.d:
ततस्तत्त्वानि सर्वाणि ध्यात्वा शिष्यतनौ न्यसेत् /
सृष्टिक्रमात् प्रकृत्यादिपृथिव्यन्तानि देशिकः //
27.m: the master should then meditate upon all the cosmic principles and deposit them in the disciple's body, / according to the order of creation, from Primordial Nature down to earth.

27.s:
tatraikadhā paṇcadhā syāddaśadvādaśadhāpi vā(4) /
:n
1 mūrtyā samprokṣya iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 sūtramiti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 tatra saṅkhyayā iti kha, ga, gha, cihnitapustakatrayapāṭhaḥ
4 nidhīyate iti gha, ṅa, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
5 tatrārcā pañcadhā yā syādaṅgair dvādaśadhāpi veti kha,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ / tatrātmā pañcadhā vā syāt
daśadvadaśadhāpiveti gha, ṅa, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
:p 73
jñātavyaḥ sarvabhedena grathitastattvacintakaiḥ //
27.d:
तत्रैकधा पण्चधा स्याद्दशद्वादशधापि वा(4) /
:न्
1 मूर्त्या सम्प्रोक्ष्य इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 सूत्रमिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 तत्र सङ्ख्यया इति ख, ग, घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकत्रयपाठः
4 निधीयते इति घ, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
5 तत्रार्चा पञ्चधा या स्यादङ्गैर् द्वादशधापि वेति ख,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः / तत्रात्मा पञ्चधा वा स्यात्
दशद्वदशधापिवेति घ, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
:प् 73
ज्ञातव्यः सर्वभेदेन ग्रथितस्तत्त्वचिन्तकैः //
27.m:
There it may be twofold, fivefold, or even tenfold or twelvefold;
[Footnote mark]
1. The reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'mūrtyā samprokṣya'.
2. The reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'sūtram'.
3. The reading in the three manuscripts marked kha, ga, and gha is 'tatra saṅkhyayā'.
4. The reading in the two manuscripts marked gha and ṅa is 'nidhīyate'.
5. The reading in the manuscript marked kha is 'tatrārcā pañcadhā yā syādaṅgair dvādaśadhāpi vā'; the reading in the two manuscripts marked gha and ṅa is 'tatrātmā pañcadhā vā syāt daśadvadaśadhāpivā'. / [Page 73]
it should be understood by contemplators of the cosmic principles as tied with all varieties.

27.s:
aṅgaiḥ pañcabhiradhvānaṃ nikhilaṃ vikṛtikramāt /
tanmātrātmani saṃhṛtya māyāsūtre paśostanau(1) //
27.d:
अङ्गैः पञ्चभिरध्वानं निखिलं विकृतिक्रमात् /
तन्मात्रात्मनि संहृत्य मायासूत्रे पशोस्तनौ(1) //
27.m: Having dissolved the entire path through the five limbs in the reverse order of cosmic transformation / into the subtle elements within the cord of illusion (māyāsūtra) on the body of the bound soul,

27.s:
prakṛtirliṅgaśaktiś ca kartā buddhis tathā manaḥ /
pañcatanmātrabuddhyākhyaṃ karmākhyaṃ bhūtapañcakaṃ //
27.d:
प्रकृतिर्लिङ्गशक्तिश् च कर्ता बुद्धिस् तथा मनः /
पञ्चतन्मात्रबुद्ध्याख्यं कर्माख्यं भूतपञ्चकं //
27.m: Prakṛti, the subtle-body power (liṅgaśakti), the agent, the intellect (buddhi), as well as the mind (manas), / the five subtle elements (tanmātra), the organs of knowledge, the organs of action, and the five gross elements—

27.s:
dhyāyecca dvādaśātmānaṃ sūtre dehe tathecchayā /
hutvā sampātavidhinā sṛṣṭeḥ sṛṣṭikrameṇa tu //
27.d:
ध्यायेच्च द्वादशात्मानं सूत्रे देहे तथेच्छया /
हुत्वा सम्पातविधिना सृष्टेः सृष्टिक्रमेण तु //
27.m: one should meditate upon the twelvefold self in the thread and in the body according to one's will. / Then, offering fire oblations according to the rule of drops (saṃpāta), in the order of creation,

27.s:
ekaikaṃ śatahomena dattvā pūrṇāhutiṃ tataḥ /
śarāve sampuṭīkṛtya kumbheśāya nivedayet //
27.d:
एकैकं शतहोमेन दत्त्वा पूर्णाहुतिं ततः /
शरावे सम्पुटीकृत्य कुम्भेशाय निवेदयेत् //
27.m: having offered a hundred fire oblations for each one, and then offering the final full oblation (pūrṇāhuti), / sealing [the thread] inside an earthen bowl, he should present it to the Lord of the Pitcher (kumbheśa).

27.s:
adhivāsya yathā nyāyaṃ bhaktaṃ śiṣyaṃ tu dīkṣayet /
karaṇīṃ kartarīṃ vāpi(2) rajāṃsi khaṭikāmapi //
27.d:
अधिवास्य यथा न्यायं भक्तं शिष्यं तु दीक्षयेत् /
करणीं कर्तरीं वापि(2) रजांसि खटिकामपि //
27.m: Having performed the preliminary consecration according to rule, he should initiate the devoted disciple. / The trowel or scissors, the powders, and the chalk—

27.s:
anyadapyupayogi syāt sarvaṃ tadvāyugocare /
saṃsthāpya mūlamantreṇa parāmṛśyādhivādhivāsayet //
27.d:
अन्यदप्युपयोगि स्यात् सर्वं तद्वायुगोचरे /
संस्थाप्य मूलमन्त्रेण परामृश्याधिवाधिवासयेत् //
27.m: and whatever else is useful—placing all that in the sphere of the wind [in the northwest], / touching them with the root mantra, he should perform the preliminary consecration.

27.s:
namo bhūtebhyaś ca baliḥ kuśe śete smaran hariṃ /
maṇḍapaṃ bhūṣayitvātha vitānaghaṭalaḍḍukaiḥ(3) //
27.d:
नमो भूतेभ्यश् च बलिः कुशे शेते स्मरन् हरिं /
मण्डपं भूषयित्वाथ वितानघटलड्डुकैः(3) //
27.m: With 'Obeisance to the beings,' a bali offering [is made], and he sleeps upon kuśa grass remembering Hari. / Then, having adorned the pavilion with canopies, pitchers, and sweets,

27.s:
maṇḍaletha yajedviṣṇuṃ tataḥ santarpya pāvakaṃ /
āhūya dīkṣayecchiṣyān baddhapadmāsanasthitān //
27.d:
मण्डलेथ यजेद्विष्णुं ततः सन्तर्प्य पावकं /
आहूय दीक्षयेच्छिष्यान् बद्धपद्मासनस्थितान् //
27.m: he should worship Viṣṇu in the maṇḍala, and then, having satisfied the fire, / he should summon and initiate the disciples who sit bound in the lotus posture.

27.s:
sammokṣya viṣṇuṃ hastena mūrdhānaṃ spṛśya vai kramāt /
prakṛtyādivikṛtyantāṃ sādhibhūtādhidaivatāṃ //
27.d:
सम्मोक्ष्य विष्णुं हस्तेन मूर्धानं स्पृश्य वै क्रमात् /
प्रकृत्यादिविकृत्यन्तां साधिभूताधिदैवतां //
27.m: Having sprinkled [them] with water for Viṣṇu and touched their heads with his hand in order, / [he contemplates] the creation beginning with prakṛti and ending with its transformations, along with the elements and deities,

27.s:
sṛṣṭimādhyātmikīṃ kṛtvā hṛdi tāṃ saṃharet kramāt /
tanmātrabhūtāṃ sakalāṃ jīvena samatāṃ gatāṃ //
27.d:
सृष्टिमाध्यात्मिकीं कृत्वा हृदि तां संहरेत् क्रमात् /
तन्मात्रभूतां सकलां जीवेन समतां गतां //
27.m: having made it interior (ādhyātmikī), he should dissolve it in order within the heart, / reduced to subtle elements and having attained identity with the individual soul (jīva).

27.s:
tataḥ samprārthya kambheśaṃ sūtraṃ saṃhṛtya deśikaḥ /
:n
1 māyāsūtre suśobhane iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 karālaṃ kartarīñcāpi iti kha, ga, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
3 vitānabhavagandhakair iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ /
vitānapaṭakendriyair iti ga, gha, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
:p 74
agneḥ samīpamāgatya pārśve taṃ sanniveśya tu //
27.d:
ततः सम्प्रार्थ्य कम्भेशं सूत्रं संहृत्य देशिकः /
:न्
1 मायासूत्रे सुशोभने इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 करालं कर्तरीञ्चापि इति ख, ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
3 वितानभवगन्धकैर् इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः /
वितानपटकेन्द्रियैर् इति ग, घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
:प् 74
अग्नेः समीपमागत्य पार्श्वे तं सन्निवेश्य तु //
27.m:
Then, praying to the Lord of the Pitcher, the preceptor gathers up the thread.
[Footnote]
1. 'In the very beautiful māyā-thread' is the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa.
2. 'The spade and the scissors' is the reading in the two manuscripts marked kha and ga.
3. 'With canopies, clothes, and fragrances' is the reading in the manuscript marked kha. / 'With canopies, banners, and flags' is the reading in the two manuscripts marked ga and gha. / [p. 74]
Coming near to the fire and seating him at its side,

27.s:
mūlamantreṇa sṛṣṭīśamāhutīnāṃ śatena taṃ /
udāsīnamathāsādya pūrṇāhutyā ca deśikaḥ //
27.d:
मूलमन्त्रेण सृष्टीशमाहुतीनां शतेन तं /
उदासीनमथासाद्य पूर्णाहुत्या च देशिकः //
27.m: the preceptor, [worshipping] the Lord of Creation with the root mantra through a hundred oblations, / then approaching him who is detached, with the final full oblation,

27.s:
śuklaṃ rajaḥ samādāya mūlena śatamantritaṃ /
santāḍya hṛdayantena huṃphaṭkārāntasaṃyutaiḥ //
27.d:
शुक्लं रजः समादाय मूलेन शतमन्त्रितं /
सन्ताड्य हृदयन्तेन हुंफट्कारान्तसंयुतैः //
27.m: taking white powder consecrated one hundred times with the root mantra, / striking [the disciple] with [the mantra ending in] hṛdaya, joined with huṃ and phaṭ at the end,

27.s:
viyogapadasaṃyuktair vījaiḥ padādibhiḥ kramāt /
pṛthivyādīni tattvāni viśliṣya juhuyāttataḥ //
27.d:
वियोगपदसंयुक्तैर् वीजैः पदादिभिः क्रमात् /
पृथिव्यादीनि तत्त्वानि विश्लिष्य जुहुयात्ततः //
27.m: with seed-syllables joined to words of severance, beginning with the words in order, / having dissociated the cosmic principles beginning with earth, he should then offer fire oblations.

27.s:
vahnāvakhilatattvānāmālaye vyāhṛte harau /
nīyamānaṃ kramātsarvaṃ tatrādhvānaṃ smaredbudhaḥ //
27.d:
वह्नावखिलतत्त्वानामालये व्याहृते हरौ /
नीयमानं क्रमात्सर्वं तत्राध्वानं स्मरेद्बुधः //
27.m: In the fire, the abode of all cosmic principles, when Hari is uttered, / the wise man should contemplate the entire path being led into it in order.

27.s:
tāḍanena viyojyaivaṃ(1) ādāyāpādya śāmyatāṃ /
prakṛtyāhṛtya juhuyādyathokte jātavedasi //
27.d:
ताडनेन वियोज्यैवं(1) आदायापाद्य शाम्यतां /
प्रकृत्याहृत्य जुहुयाद्यथोक्ते जातवेदसि //
27.m: Severing thus by striking, taking it, and bringing it to pacification, / drawing it into prakṛti, he should offer it into the fire as prescribed.

27.s: garbhādhānaṃ jātakarma bhogañcaiva layantathā /
27.d: गर्भाधानं जातकर्म भोगञ्चैव लयन्तथा /
27.m: Conception, the birth-rite, experience, and likewise dissolution:

27.s:
śuddhaṃ tattvaṃ samuddhṛtya pūrṇāhutyā tu deśikaḥ /
sannayeddvipare tattve yāvadavyāhṛtaṃ kramāt //
27.d:
शुद्धं तत्त्वं समुद्धृत्य पूर्णाहुत्या तु देशिकः /
सन्नयेद्द्विपरे तत्त्वे यावदव्याहृतं क्रमात् //
27.m: raising up the purified cosmic principle, the preceptor, by means of the final full oblation, / should lead it into the higher cosmic principle in order, up to the unmanifest.

27.s:
tat paraṃ jñānayogena vilāpya paramātmani /
vimuktabandhanaṃ jīvaṃ parasminnavyaye pade //
27.d:
तत् परं ज्ञानयोगेन विलाप्य परमात्मनि /
विमुक्तबन्धनं जीवं परस्मिन्नव्यये पदे //
27.m: Having dissolved that highest principle into the supreme self through the yoga of knowledge, / the wise man should contemplate the soul, freed from bonds, in the supreme imperishable state,

27.s:
nivṛttaṃ paramānande śuddhe buddhe smaredbudhaḥ /
dadyāt pūrṇāhutiṃ paścādevaṃ dīkṣā samāpyate //
27.d:
निवृत्तं परमानन्दे शुद्धे बुद्धे स्मरेद्बुधः /
दद्यात् पूर्णाहुतिं पश्चादेवं दीक्षा समाप्यते //
27.m: withdrawn into supreme bliss, pure, and enlightened. / He should then give the final full oblation; thus the initiation is completed.

27.s:
prayogamantrān vakṣyāmi yair dīkṣā homasaṃlayaḥ /
oṃ yaṃ bhūtāni viśuddhaṃ huṃ phaṭ
anena tāḍanaṃ kuryādviyojanamiha dvayaṃ //
27.d:
प्रयोगमन्त्रान् वक्ष्यामि यैर् दीक्षा होमसंलयः /
ओं यं भूतानि विशुद्धं हुं फट्
अनेन ताडनं कुर्याद्वियोजनमिह द्वयं //
27.m:
I shall state the practical mantras through which initiation and dissolution in the fire [occur]:
Oṃ yaṃ bhūtāni viśuddhaṃ huṃ phaṭ.
With this he should perform both the striking and the severance here.

27.s:
oṃ yaṃ bhūtānyāpātayehaṃ
ādānaṃ kṛtvā cānena prakṛtyā yojanaṃ śṛṇu /
:n
1 tāḍanena vimokṣyaivamiti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 75
oṃ yaṃ bhūtāni puṃścāho
homamantraṃ pravakṣyāmi tataḥ pūrṇāhutermanuṃ //
oṃ bhūtāni saṃhara svāhā / oṃ aṃ oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya
vauṣaṭ
27.d:
ओं यं भूतान्यापातयेहं
आदानं कृत्वा चानेन प्रकृत्या योजनं शृणु /
:न्
1 ताडनेन विमोक्ष्यैवमिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 75
ओं यं भूतानि पुंश्चाहो
होममन्त्रं प्रवक्ष्यामि ततः पूर्णाहुतेर्मनुं //
ओं भूतानि संहर स्वाहा / ओं अं ओं नमो भगवते वासुदेवाय
वौषट्
27.m:
'Oṃ yaṃ bhūtāny āpātaye 'ham'— / having performed the taking with this, hear the union with prakṛti:
[Footnote]
1. 'Thus releasing by striking' is the reading in the manuscript marked kha. / [p. 75]
Oṃ yaṃ bhūtāni puṃścāho. / I shall state the mantra of the oblation, and then the mantra of the final full oblation:
Oṃ bhūtāni saṃhara svāhā. / Oṃ aṃ oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya vauṣaṭ.

27.s:
pūrṇāhutyanantare tu tadvai śiṣyantu sādhayet(1) /
evaṃ tattvāni sarvāṇi kramātsaṃśodhayed budhaḥ //
27.d:
पूर्णाहुत्यनन्तरे तु तद्वै शिष्यन्तु साधयेत्(1) /
एवं तत्त्वानि सर्वाणि क्रमात्संशोधयेद् बुधः //
27.m: Immediately after the final full oblation, he should bring the disciple into that [higher principle]. / In this way the wise man should purify all cosmic principles in order,

27.s:
namontena svavījena tāḍanādipuraḥsaram /
oṃ vāṃ varmendriyāṇi / oṃ deṃ buddhīndriyāṇi
yaṃ vījena samānantu tāḍanādiprayogakam //
27.d:
नमोन्तेन स्ववीजेन ताडनादिपुरःसरम् /
ओं वां वर्मेन्द्रियाणि / ओं दें बुद्धीन्द्रियाणि
यं वीजेन समानन्तु ताडनादिप्रयोगकम् //
27.m:
beginning with striking and so forth, with each one's own seed-syllable ending in namaḥ.
Oṃ vāṃ karmendriyāṇi; Oṃ deṃ buddhīndriyāṇi.
The application of striking and so forth is similar, with the seed-syllable yaṃ:

27.s:
oṃ suṃgandhatanmātre viyuṅkṣva huṃ phaṭ / oṃ sampāhiṃ
hā(2) // oṃ khaṃ khaṃ kṣa prakṛtyā(3) / oṃ suṃ huṃ
gandhatanmātre saṃhara svāhā
tataḥ pūrṇāhutiś caivamuttareṣu prayujyate /
oṃ rāṃ rasatanmātre / oṃ bheṃ rūpatanmātre / oṃ raṃ
sparśatanmātre / oṃ eṃ śabdatanmātre / oṃ bhaṃ namaḥ / oṃ
soṃ ahaṅkāraḥ / oṃ naṃ buddhe / oṃ oṃ prakṛte
ekamūrtāvayaṃ prokto dīkṣāyogaḥ samāsataḥ /
evameva prayogastu navavyūhādike smṛtaḥ //
27.d:
ओं सुंगन्धतन्मात्रे वियुङ्क्ष्व हुं फट् / ओं सम्पाहिं
हा(2) // ओं खं खं क्ष प्रकृत्या(3) / ओं सुं हुं
गन्धतन्मात्रे संहर स्वाहा
ततः पूर्णाहुतिश् चैवमुत्तरेषु प्रयुज्यते /
ओं रां रसतन्मात्रे / ओं भें रूपतन्मात्रे / ओं रं
स्पर्शतन्मात्रे / ओं एं शब्दतन्मात्रे / ओं भं नमः / ओं
सों अहङ्कारः / ओं नं बुद्धे / ओं ओं प्रकृते
एकमूर्तावयं प्रोक्तो दीक्षायोगः समासतः /
एवमेव प्रयोगस्तु नवव्यूहादिके स्मृतः //
27.m:
Oṃ suṃ gandhatanmātre viyuṅkṣva huṃ phaṭ. Oṃ saṃ pāhi hā. Oṃ khaṃ khaṃ kṣa prakṛtyā. Oṃ suṃ huṃ gandhatanmātre saṃhara svāhā. / Then the final full oblation is applied in this manner to the subsequent ones:
Oṃ rāṃ rasatanmātre; Oṃ bheṃ rūpatanmātre; Oṃ raṃ sparśatanmātre; Oṃ eṃ śabdatanmātre; Oṃ bhaṃ namaḥ; Oṃ soṃ ahaṅkāraḥ; Oṃ naṃ buddhe; Oṃ oṃ prakṛte.
This practice of initiation is declared briefly in the case of a single icon;
in this very manner is the practice taught for the ninefold manifestation (navavyūha) and the rest.

27.s:
dagdhāparasmin sandadhyānnirvāṇe prakṛtinnaraḥ /
avikāre samādadhyādīśvare prakṛtinnaraḥ //
27.d:
दग्धापरस्मिन् सन्दध्यान्निर्वाणे प्रकृतिन्नरः /
अविकारे समादध्यादीश्वरे प्रकृतिन्नरः //
27.m: Having burned it, a man should join prakṛti to the supreme in liberating initiation (nirvāṇa); / a man should establish prakṛti in the changeless Lord (īśvara).

27.s:
śodhayitvātha bhutāni karmāṅgāni(4) viśodhayet /
buddhyākhyānyatha tanmātramanojñānamahaṅkṛtiṃ //
27.d:
शोधयित्वाथ भुतानि कर्माङ्गानि(4) विशोधयेत् /
बुद्ध्याख्यान्यथ तन्मात्रमनोज्ञानमहङ्कृतिं //
27.m: Having purified the gross elements, he should then purify the organs of action, / then the organs of knowledge, the subtle elements, the mind, intellect, ego,

27.s:
liṅgātmānaṃ viśodhyānte prakṛtiṃ śodhāyet punaḥ /
:n
1 tadvai śiṣyantusannayediti kha, gha, ṅa,
cihnitapustakatrayapāṭhaḥ
2 oṃ suṃ āyāhi hāmiti kha,cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ oṃ saṃ pāhi
svāhā iti ga, ṅa, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
3 aṃ duṃ stva prakṛtyā iti oṃ khaṃ khaṃ stva prakṛtyā iti ca kha,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
4 karmākhyāni ca śodhayediti gha, ṅa, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
:p 76
puruṣaṃ prākṛtaṃ śuddhamīśvare dhāmni saṃsthitaṃ //
27.d:
लिङ्गात्मानं विशोध्यान्ते प्रकृतिं शोधायेत् पुनः /
:न्
1 तद्वै शिष्यन्तुसन्नयेदिति ख, घ, ङ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकत्रयपाठः
2 ओं सुं आयाहि हामिति ख,चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः ओं सं पाहि
स्वाहा इति ग, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
3 अं दुं स्त्व प्रकृत्या इति ओं खं खं स्त्व प्रकृत्या इति च ख,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
4 कर्माख्यानि च शोधयेदिति घ, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
:प् 76
पुरुषं प्राकृतं शुद्धमीश्वरे धाम्नि संस्थितं //
27.m:
and having purified the nature of the subtle body, he should at the end purify prakṛti again.
[Footnote]
1. 'He should truly lead the disciple into that' is the reading in the three manuscripts marked kha, gha, and ṅa.
2. 'Oṃ suṃ āyāhi hām' is the reading in the manuscript marked kha; 'Oṃ saṃ pāhi svāhā' is the reading in the two manuscripts marked ga and ṅa.
3. 'Aṃ duṃ stva prakṛtyā' and 'Oṃ khaṃ khaṃ stva prakṛtyā' is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
4. 'And he should purify the organs of action' is the reading in the two manuscripts marked gha and ṅa. / [p. 76]
The spiritual person (puruṣa) freed from nature (prākṛta), purified, established in the abode of the Lord,

27.s:
svagocarīkṛtāśeṣabhogamuktau kṛtāspadaṃ /
dhyāyan pūrṇāhutiṃ dadyāddīkṣeyaṃ tvadhikāriṇī //
27.d:
स्वगोचरीकृताशेषभोगमुक्तौ कृतास्पदं /
ध्यायन् पूर्णाहुतिं दद्याद्दीक्षेयं त्वधिकारिणी //
27.m: who has made the entire field of experience his own and established himself in liberation— / contemplating him, he should offer the final full oblation. This is the qualifying initiation (adhikāriṇī dīkṣā).

27.s:
aṅgair ārādhya mantrasya nītvā tattvagaṇaṃ samaṃ /
kramādevaṃ viśodhyānte sarvasiddhisamanvitaṃ //
27.d:
अङ्गैर् आराध्य मन्त्रस्य नीत्वा तत्त्वगणं समं /
क्रमादेवं विशोध्यान्ते सर्वसिद्धिसमन्वितं //
27.m: Having worshipped with the limbs of the mantra, bringing the group of cosmic principles into equilibrium, / purifying them in order thus at the end, endowed with all supernatural attainments (siddhi),

27.s:
dhyāyan pūrṇāhitiṃ dadyātdīkṣeyaṃ sādhake smṛtā /
dravyasya vā na sampattiraśaktirvātmano yadi //
27.d:
ध्यायन् पूर्णाहितिं दद्यात्दीक्षेयं साधके स्मृता /
द्रव्यस्य वा न सम्पत्तिरशक्तिर्वात्मनो यदि //
27.m: contemplating, he should offer the final full oblation. This initiation is taught for the practitioner (sādhaka). / If there is lack of wealth or incapacity of oneself,

27.s:
iṣṭvā devaṃ yathā pūrvaṃ sarvopakaraṇānvitaṃ /
sadyodhivāsya dvādaśyāṃ dīkṣayeddeśikottamaḥ //
27.d:
इष्ट्वा देवं यथा पूर्वं सर्वोपकरणान्वितं /
सद्योधिवास्य द्वादश्यां दीक्षयेद्देशिकोत्तमः //
27.m: having worshipped the deity as before with all the ritual implements, / performing the preliminary consecration immediately, the excellent preceptor should initiate on the twelfth lunar day (dvādaśī).

27.s:
bhakto vinītaḥ śārīrair guṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ samanvitaḥ /
śiṣyo nātidhanī yastu sthaṇḍilebhyarcya dīkṣayet //
27.d:
भक्तो विनीतः शारीरैर् गुणैः सर्वैः समन्वितः /
शिष्यो नातिधनी यस्तु स्थण्डिलेभ्यर्च्य दीक्षयेत् //
27.m: A disciple who is devoted, humble, endowed with all physical virtues, / but not very wealthy, he should initiate after worshipping upon a bare sacrificial ground (sthaṇḍila).

27.s:
adhvānaṃ nikhilaṃ daivaṃ(2) bhautaṃ vādhyātmikī kṛtaṃ /
sṛṣṭikrameṇa śiṣyasya dehe dhyātvā tu deśikaḥ //
27.d:
अध्वानं निखिलं दैवं(2) भौतं वाध्यात्मिकी कृतं /
सृष्टिक्रमेण शिष्यस्य देहे ध्यात्वा तु देशिकः //
27.m: The entire cosmic path—divine, elemental, or made internal— / meditating upon it in the order of creation within the disciple's body, the preceptor,

27.s:
aṣṭāṣṭāhutibhiḥ pūrvaṃ kramāt santarpya sṛṣṭimān /
svamantrair vāsudevādīn jananādīn visarjayet(2) //
27.d:
अष्टाष्टाहुतिभिः पूर्वं क्रमात् सन्तर्प्य सृष्टिमान् /
स्वमन्त्रैर् वासुदेवादीन् जननादीन् विसर्जयेत्(2) //
27.m: having first propitiated with eight oblations each in order, observing the order of creation, / should dismiss Vāsudeva and the others, birth and the other [rites], with their own mantras.

27.s:
homena śodhayet paścātsaṃhārakramayogataḥ /
yonisūtrāṇi baddhāni muktvā karmāṇi deśikaḥ //
27.d:
होमेन शोधयेत् पश्चात्संहारक्रमयोगतः /
योनिसूत्राणि बद्धानि मुक्त्वा कर्माणि देशिकः //
27.m: He should afterwards purify through fire oblations by applying the order of dissolution; / having released the tied threads of origin and the karmas, the preceptor

27.s:
śiṣyadehātsamāhṛtya kramāttattvāni śodhayet /
agnau prākṛtike viṣṇau layaṃ nītvādhidaivake //
27.d:
शिष्यदेहात्समाहृत्य क्रमात्तत्त्वानि शोधयेत् /
अग्नौ प्राकृतिके विष्णौ लयं नीत्वाधिदैवके //
27.m: Withdrawing the principles from the disciple's body, he should purify them in sequence, / having dissolved them into the fire belonging to Prakṛti, [and] into Viṣṇu, the presiding deity.

27.s:
śuddhaṃ tattvamaśuddhena pūrṇāhutyā tu sādhayet(3) /
śiṣye prakṛtimāpanne dagdhvā prākṛtikān guṇān //
:n
1 likhitaṃ daivamiti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 pūjāṃ kṛtvā visarjayediti gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ vimalādīn
visarjayediti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 pūrṇāhutyā tu sannayediti kha, gha, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
:p 77
27.d:
शुद्धं तत्त्वमशुद्धेन पूर्णाहुत्या तु साधयेत्(3) /
शिष्ये प्रकृतिमापन्ने दग्ध्वा प्राकृतिकान् गुणान् //
:न्
1 लिखितं दैवमिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 पूजां कृत्वा विसर्जयेदिति घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः विमलादीन्
विसर्जयेदिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 पूर्णाहुत्या तु सन्नयेदिति ख, घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
:प् 77
27.m:
With a full offering, he should effect the pure principle by means of the impure, / and once the disciple has attained the state of Prakṛti, having burnt away the qualities belonging to Prakṛti,
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: The manuscript marked kha reads 'likhitaṃ daivam'.]
[Footnote 2: The manuscript marked gha reads 'pūjāṃ kṛtvā visarjayet'; the manuscript marked ṅa reads 'vimalādīn visarjayet'.]
[Footnote 3: The two manuscripts marked kha and gha read 'pūrṇāhutyā tu sannayet'. / p. 77]

27.s:
maucayedadhikāre vā niyuñjyāddeśikaḥ śiśūn(1) /
athānyān śaktidīkṣāṃ vā kuryāt bhāve sthito guruḥ //
27.d:
मौचयेदधिकारे वा नियुञ्ज्याद्देशिकः शिशून्(1) /
अथान्यान् शक्तिदीक्षां वा कुर्यात् भावे स्थितो गुरुः //
27.m: the master should release or assign the youngsters to their qualification; / or, established in devotional contemplation, the guru may perform the initiation of power for others.

27.s:
bhaktyā samprātipannānāṃ yatīnāṃ nirdhanasya ca /
sampūjya sthaṇḍile viṣṇuṃ pārśvasthaṃ sthāpya putrakaṃ //
27.d:
भक्त्या सम्प्रातिपन्नानां यतीनां निर्धनस्य च /
सम्पूज्य स्थण्डिले विष्णुं पार्श्वस्थं स्थाप्य पुत्रकं //
27.m: For those who have surrendered out of devotion, for ascetics, and for a poor man, / having worshipped Viṣṇu on an earthen altar, placing the spiritual son beside him,

27.s:
devatābhimukhaḥ śiṣyastiryagāsyaḥ svayaṃ sthitaḥ /
adhvānaṃ nikhilaṃ dhyātvā parvabhiḥ svair vikalpitaṃ //
27.d:
देवताभिमुखः शिष्यस्तिर्यगास्यः स्वयं स्थितः /
अध्वानं निखिलं ध्यात्वा पर्वभिः स्वैर् विकल्पितं //
27.m: the disciple facing the deity, while he himself sits turned sideways, / having meditated upon the entire path divided according to its sections,

27.s:
śiṣyadehe tathā devamādhidaivikayācanaṃ /
dhyānayogena sañcintya pūrvavattāḍanādinā //
27.d:
शिष्यदेहे तथा देवमाधिदैविकयाचनं /
ध्यानयोगेन सञ्चिन्त्य पूर्ववत्ताडनादिना //
27.m: and contemplating through meditative union the deity in the disciple's body, the petition to the presiding deity, / as before, by means of striking and the rest,

27.s:
kramāttattvāni sarvāṇi śodhayet sthaṇḍile harau /
tāḍanena viyojyātha gṛhītvātmani tatparaḥ(2) //
27.d:
क्रमात्तत्त्वानि सर्वाणि शोधयेत् स्थण्डिले हरौ /
ताडनेन वियोज्याथ गृहीत्वात्मनि तत्परः(2) //
27.m: he should purify all the principles in order upon Hari on the earthen altar. / Having detached [a principle] by striking, and having taken it into himself, intent on that,

27.s:
deve saṃyojya saṃśodhya gṛhītvā tat svabhāvataḥ /
ānīya śuddhabhāvena sandhayitvā krameṇa tu //
27.d:
देवे संयोज्य संशोध्य गृहीत्वा तत् स्वभावतः /
आनीय शुद्धभावेन सन्धयित्वा क्रमेण तु //
27.m: uniting it with the deity, purifying it, taking it back naturally, / bringing it in a pure state, and joining it in sequence,

27.s:
śodhayeddhyānayogena sarvato jñānamudrayā /
śuddheṣu sarvatattveṣu pradhāne ceśvare sthite //
27.d:
शोधयेद्ध्यानयोगेन सर्वतो ज्ञानमुद्रया /
शुद्धेषु सर्वतत्त्वेषु प्रधाने चेश्वरे स्थिते //
27.m: he should purify [it] completely through meditative union with the gesture of wisdom. / When all principles are purified, and Pradhāna rests in the Lord,

27.s:
dagdhvā nirvāpayecchiṣyān pade caiśe niyojayet /
ninayet siddhimārge vā sādhakaṃ deśikottamaḥ //
27.d:
दग्ध्वा निर्वापयेच्छिष्यान् पदे चैशे नियोजयेत् /
निनयेत् सिद्धिमार्गे वा साधकं देशिकोत्तमः //
27.m: having burnt [the bonds], he should liberate the disciples and establish [them] in the state of the Lord; / or the excellent master should lead the practitioner onto the path of spiritual attainments.

27.s:
evamevādhikārastho gṛhī karmaṇyatandritaḥ /
ātmānaṃ śodhayaṃstiṣṭhed yāvadrāgakṣayo bhavet //
27.d:
एवमेवाधिकारस्थो गृही कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः /
आत्मानं शोधयंस्तिष्ठेद् यावद्रागक्षयो भवेत् //
27.m: Thus established in his qualification, unwearied in rites, a householder / should remain purifying himself until his attachment is destroyed.

27.s:
kṣīṇarāgamathātmānaṃ jñātvā saṃśuddhikilviṣaḥ /
āropya putre śiṣye vā hy adhikārantu saṃyamī //
27.d:
क्षीणरागमथात्मानं ज्ञात्वा संशुद्धिकिल्विषः /
आरोप्य पुत्रे शिष्ये वा ह्य् अधिकारन्तु संयमी //
27.m: Knowing himself to be free of attachment, with his sins thoroughly purified, / having transferred his authority onto his son or disciple, the self-controlled man,

27.s:
dagdhvā māyāmayaṃ pāśaṃ pravrajya svātmani sthitaḥ /
śarīrapātamākāṅkṣannāsītāvyaktaliṅgavān //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye sarvadīkṣākathanaṃ nāma
saptaviṃśodhyāyaḥ
:n
1 paśūniti gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 tat punariti kha, ga, gha, ṅa, cihnitapustakacatuṣṭayapāṭhaḥ
:p 78
:ś atha aṣṭāviṃśodhyāyaḥ
abhiṣekavidhānaṃ
27.d:
दग्ध्वा मायामयं पाशं प्रव्रज्य स्वात्मनि स्थितः /
शरीरपातमाकाङ्क्षन्नासीताव्यक्तलिङ्गवान् //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये सर्वदीक्षाकथनं नाम
सप्तविंशोध्यायः
:न्
1 पशूनिति घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 तत् पुनरिति ख, ग, घ, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकचतुष्टयपाठः
:प् 78
:श् अथ अष्टाविंशोध्यायः
अभिषेकविधानं
27.m:
having burnt the snare made of Māyā, having renounced, remaining in himself, / awaiting the fall of his body, should abide without outward sectarian marks.
Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, entitled 'The Explanation of All Initiations', in the venerable Mahāpurāṇa composed by Agni.
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: The manuscript marked gha reads 'paśūn'.]
[Footnote 2: The four manuscripts marked kha, ga, gha, and ṅa read 'tat punar'. / p. 78]
Now the twenty-eighth chapter.
The Procedure for Consecration by Aspersion

28.s:
nārada uvāca
abhiṣekaṃ pravakṣyāmi yathācāryastu putrakaḥ /
siddhibhāk sādhako yena rogī rogādvimucyate //
28.d:
नारद उवाच
अभिषेकं प्रवक्ष्यामि यथाचार्यस्तु पुत्रकः /
सिद्धिभाक् साधको येन रोगी रोगाद्विमुच्यते //
28.m: Nārada said: / I shall explain the consecration by aspersion whereby the spiritual son becomes an ācārya, / the practitioner enjoys spiritual attainment, and the diseased man is freed from illness.

28.s:
rājyaṃ rājā sutaṃ strīñca prāpnuyānmalanāśanaṃ /
mūrtikumbhān suratnāḍhyānmadhyapūrvādito nyaset //
28.d:
राज्यं राजा सुतं स्त्रीञ्च प्राप्नुयान्मलनाशनं /
मूर्तिकुम्भान् सुरत्नाढ्यान्मध्यपूर्वादितो न्यसेत् //
28.m: A king obtains a kingdom, a woman a son; and it destroys impurities. / One should place the pitchers representing the deities, rich in fine jewels, beginning from the center and the east.

28.s:
sahasrāvartitān kuryādathavā śatavartitān /
maṇḍape maṇḍale viṣṇuṃ prācyaiśānyāñca pīṭhike //
28.d:
सहस्रावर्तितान् कुर्यादथवा शतवर्तितान् /
मण्डपे मण्डले विष्णुं प्राच्यैशान्याञ्च पीठिके //
28.m: He should recite over them a thousand times or a hundred times. / In a pavilion, upon a maṇḍala, [having established] Viṣṇu on the pedestal in the east and northeast,

28.s:
niveśya śakalīkṛtya putrakaṃ sādhakādikaṃ /
abhiṣekaṃ samabhyarcya kuryādgītādipūrvakaṃ //
28.d:
निवेश्य शकलीकृत्य पुत्रकं साधकादिकं /
अभिषेकं समभ्यर्च्य कुर्याद्गीतादिपूर्वकं //
28.m: having seated the spiritual son, the practitioner, and others, and having performed the division of the body, / having worshipped, he should perform the consecration by aspersion, preceded by singing and the rest.

28.s:
dadyācca yogapīṭhādīṃstvanugrāhyāstvayā narāḥ /
guruś ca samayān brūyādguptaḥ śiṣyotha sarvabhāk //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye ācāryābhiṣeko nāma
aṣṭāviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha ūnatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
sarvatobhadramaṇḍalakathanaṃ
28.d:
दद्याच्च योगपीठादींस्त्वनुग्राह्यास्त्वया नराः /
गुरुश् च समयान् ब्रूयाद्गुप्तः शिष्योथ सर्वभाक् //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये आचार्याभिषेको नाम
अष्टाविंशो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ ऊनत्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
सर्वतोभद्रमण्डलकथनं
28.m:
And he should give the throne of yoga and other [insignia], saying, 'People must be favored by you.' / And the guru should declare the pledges; then the disciple, protected, attains all.
Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter, entitled 'Consecration of the Ācārya by Aspersion', in the venerable Mahāpurāṇa composed by Agni.
Now the twenty-ninth chapter.
The Explanation of the Sarvatobhadra Maṇḍala

29.s:
nārada uvāca
sādhakaḥ sādhayenmantraṃ devatāyatanādike /
śuddhabhūmau gṛhe prārcya maṇḍale harimīśvaraṃ //
29.d:
नारद उवाच
साधकः साधयेन्मन्त्रं देवतायतनादिके /
शुद्धभूमौ गृहे प्रार्च्य मण्डले हरिमीश्वरं //
29.m: Nārada said: / The practitioner should master the mantra in an abode of the deity or similar place, / on pure ground, or in a house, having first worshipped Hari, the Supreme Lord, in a maṇḍala.

29.s:
caturastrīkṛte kṣetre maṇḍalādīni vai likhet /
rasavāṇākṣikoṣṭheṣu sarvatobhadramālikhet //
29.d:
चतुरस्त्रीकृते क्षेत्रे मण्डलादीनि वै लिखेत् /
रसवाणाक्षिकोष्ठेषु सर्वतोभद्रमालिखेत् //
29.m: In a field made square, he should draw maṇḍalas and the like. / In two hundred and fifty-six compartments, he should draw the Sarvatobhadra [maṇḍala].

29.s:
ṣaṭtriṃśatkoṣṭhakaiḥ padmaṃ pīṭhaṃ paṅktyāvahirbhavet /
dvābhyāntu vīthikā tasmād dvābhyāṃ dvārāṇi dikṣu ca //
:p 79
29.d:
षट्त्रिंशत्कोष्ठकैः पद्मं पीठं पङ्क्त्यावहिर्भवेत् /
द्वाभ्यान्तु वीथिका तस्माद् द्वाभ्यां द्वाराणि दिक्षु च //
:प् 79
29.m:
The lotus consists of thirty-six compartments; outside it, in a row, is the seat; / next is a pathway of two [rows], and in the cardinal directions are doors measuring two [compartments].
p. 79

29.s:
vartulaṃ bhrāmayitvā tu padmakṣetraṃ puroditam /
padmārdhe bhāmayitvā tu bhāgaṃ dvādaśamaṃ vahiḥ //
29.d:
वर्तुलं भ्रामयित्वा तु पद्मक्षेत्रं पुरोदितम् /
पद्मार्धे भामयित्वा तु भागं द्वादशमं वहिः //
29.m: Having inscribed a circle within the lotus-field previously mentioned, / having rotated it at half of the lotus, [and] leaving the twelfth part outside,

29.s:
vibhajya bhrāmayeccheṣaṃ catuḥkṣetrantu vartulaṃ /
prathamaṃ karṇikākṣetraṃ keśarāṇāṃ dvitīyakam //
29.d:
विभज्य भ्रामयेच्छेषं चतुःक्षेत्रन्तु वर्तुलं /
प्रथमं कर्णिकाक्षेत्रं केशराणां द्वितीयकम् //
29.m: dividing it, he should draw the remaining circular field of four zones. / The first is the field of the pericarp; the second is that of the filaments;

29.s:
tṛtīyaṃ dalasandhīnāṃ dalāgrāṇāṃ caturthakam /
prasārya koṇasūtrāṇi koṇadiṅmadhyamantataḥ //
29.d:
तृतीयं दलसन्धीनां दलाग्राणां चतुर्थकम् /
प्रसार्य कोणसूत्राणि कोणदिङ्मध्यमन्ततः //
29.m: the third is that of the petal joints; the fourth is that of the petal tips. / Stretching the corner cords, and having placed the ends / at the midpoint between the corners and directions on the tips of the filaments, he should mark the petal joints. / Then, having dropped the cords, he should draw the eight petals there.

29.s:
nidhāya keśarāgre tu dalasandhīṃstu lāñchayet /
pātayitvātha sūtrāṇi tatra patrāṣṭakaṃ likhet //
29.d:
निधाय केशराग्रे तु दलसन्धींस्तु लाञ्छयेत् /
पातयित्वाथ सूत्राणि तत्र पत्राष्टकं लिखेत् //
29.m: Then, having dropped the cords, he should draw the eight petals there.

29.s:
dalasandhyantarālantu mānaṃ madhye nidhāya tu /
dalāgraṃ bhrāmayettena tadagraṃ tadanantaraṃ //
29.d:
दलसन्ध्यन्तरालन्तु मानं मध्ये निधाय तु /
दलाग्रं भ्रामयेत्तेन तदग्रं तदनन्तरं //
29.m: Placing the measure of the interval between the petal joints in the center, / he should rotate the tip of the petal with it, and immediately thereafter its apex.

29.s:
tadantarālaṃ tatpārśve kṛtvā vāhyakrameṇa ca /
keśare tu likheddvau dvau dalamadhye tataḥ punaḥ //
29.d:
तदन्तरालं तत्पार्श्वे कृत्वा वाह्यक्रमेण च /
केशरे तु लिखेद्द्वौ द्वौ दलमध्ये ततः पुनः //
29.m: Placing that interval on its sides, and in an outward order, / he should draw two filaments each in the middle of each petal.

29.s:
padmalakṣmaitat sāmānyaṃ dviṣaṭkadalamucyate /
karṇikārdhena mānena prāksaṃsthaṃ bhrāmayet kramāt //
29.d:
पद्मलक्ष्मैतत् सामान्यं द्विषट्कदलमुच्यते /
कर्णिकार्धेन मानेन प्राक्संस्थं भ्रामयेत् क्रमात् //
29.m: This is the general characteristic of the lotus; it is called twelve-petalled. / With a measure equal to half of the pericarp, he should rotate in order from the east.

29.s:
tatpārśve bhramayogena kuṇḍalyaḥ ṣaḍ bhavanti hi /
evaṃ dvādaśa matsyāḥ syurdviṣaṭkadalakañca taiḥ //
29.d:
तत्पार्श्वे भ्रमयोगेन कुण्डल्यः षड् भवन्ति हि /
एवं द्वादश मत्स्याः स्युर्द्विषट्कदलकञ्च तैः //
29.m: On its side, by the motion of the compass, there are indeed six coils; / thus there are twelve fish figures, and through them is the twelve-petalled [lotus].

29.s:
pañcapatrābhisiddhyarthaṃ matsyaṃ kṛtvaivamabjakam /
vyomarekhāvahiḥ pīṭhantatra koṣṭāni mārjayet //
29.d:
पञ्चपत्राभिसिद्ध्यर्थं मत्स्यं कृत्वैवमब्जकम् /
व्योमरेखावहिः पीठन्तत्र कोष्टानि मार्जयेत् //
29.m: For the accomplishment of the five-petalled lotus, having made the fish figure thus for the lotus, / outside the sky-line is the pedestal; there he should clear the compartments:

29.s:
trīṇi koṇeṣu pādārthaṃ dvidvikānyaparāṇi tu /
caturdikṣu viliptāni gātrakāṇi bhavantyuta //
29.d:
त्रीणि कोणेषु पादार्थं द्विद्विकान्यपराणि तु /
चतुर्दिक्षु विलिप्तानि गात्रकाणि भवन्त्युत //
29.m: three in the corners for the feet, and the others in pairs; / coated in the four directions, they become the limbs.

29.s:
tataḥ paṅktidvayaṃ dikṣu vīṭhyarthantu vilopayet(1) /
dvārāṇyāśāsu kurvīta catvāri catasṛṣvapi //
29.d:
ततः पङ्क्तिद्वयं दिक्षु वीठ्यर्थन्तु विलोपयेत्(1) /
द्वाराण्याशासु कुर्वीत चत्वारि चतसृष्वपि //
29.m: Then he should erase two rows in the directions for the sake of the pathway; / he should make four doors in all four directions.

29.s:
dvārāṇāṃ pārśvataḥ śobhā aṣṭau kuryādvicakṣaṇaḥ /
:n
1 paṅktidvayaṃ dvayaṃ dikṣu vīthyarthaṃ viniyojayediti ṅa,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 80
tatpārśva upaśobhāstu tāvatyaḥ parikīrtitāḥ //
29.d:
द्वाराणां पार्श्वतः शोभा अष्टौ कुर्याद्विचक्षणः /
:न्
1 पङ्क्तिद्वयं द्वयं दिक्षु वीथ्यर्थं विनियोजयेदिति ङ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 80
तत्पार्श्व उपशोभास्तु तावत्यः परिकीर्तिताः //
29.m:
On the sides of the doors, the wise man should make eight decorative projections.
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: The manuscript marked ṅa reads 'paṅktidvayaṃ dvayaṃ dikṣu vīthyarthaṃ viniyojayet'. / p. 80]
Beside them, as many subsidiary projections are proclaimed.

29.s:
samīpa upaśobhānāṃ koṇāstu parikīrtitāḥ(1) /
caturdikṣu tato dve dve cintayenmadhyakoṣṭhakaiḥ //
29.d:
समीप उपशोभानां कोणास्तु परिकीर्तिताः(1) /
चतुर्दिक्षु ततो द्वे द्वे चिन्तयेन्मध्यकोष्ठकैः //
29.m: Near the subsidiary projections, corners are proclaimed; / from there, in the four directions, he should design two [compartments] each from the central compartments.

29.s:
catvāri vāhyato mṛjyādekaikaṃ pārśvayorapi /
śobhārthaṃ pārśvayostrīṇi trīṇi lumpaddalasya tu //
29.d:
चत्वारि वाह्यतो मृज्यादेकैकं पार्श्वयोरपि /
शोभार्थं पार्श्वयोस्त्रीणि त्रीणि लुम्पद्दलस्य तु //
29.m: He should wipe out four on the outside, and one on each of the two sides; / for the sake of the decorative projection, he should erase three on each side of the petal.

29.s:
tadvadviparyaye kuryādupaśobhāṃ tataḥ param /
koṇasyāntarvahistrīṇi cintayeddvirvibhedataḥ //
29.d:
तद्वद्विपर्यये कुर्यादुपशोभां ततः परम् /
कोणस्यान्तर्वहिस्त्रीणि चिन्तयेद्द्विर्विभेदतः //
29.m: In the same inverted manner, he should then make the subsidiary projection. / Inside and outside the corner, he should design three by a twofold division.

29.s:
evaṃ ṣoḍaśakoṣṭhaṃ syādevamanyattu maṇḍalam /
dviṣaṭkabhāge ṣaṭtriṃśatpadaṃ padmantu vīthikā //
29.d:
एवं षोडशकोष्ठं स्यादेवमन्यत्तु मण्डलम् /
द्विषट्कभागे षट्त्रिंशत्पदं पद्मन्तु वीथिका //
29.m: Thus it becomes sixteen compartments; thus is another maṇḍala. / In a division of twelve, the lotus has thirty-six squares, while the pathway

29.s:
ekā paṅktiḥ prābhyāṃ tu dvāraśobhādi pūrvavat /
dvādaśāṅgulibhiḥ padmamekahaste tu maṇḍale //
29.d:
एका पङ्क्तिः प्राभ्यां तु द्वारशोभादि पूर्ववत् /
द्वादशाङ्गुलिभिः पद्ममेकहस्ते तु मण्डले //
29.m: is one row; with two rows are the door, decorative projection, and the rest, as before. / In a maṇḍala of one cubit, the lotus is twelve finger-breadths;

29.s:
dvihaste hastamātraṃ syādvṛddhyā dvāreṇa vācaret /
apīṭhañcaturasraṃ syādvikarañcakrapaṅkajam //
29.d:
द्विहस्ते हस्तमात्रं स्याद्वृद्ध्या द्वारेण वाचरेत् /
अपीठञ्चतुरस्रं स्याद्विकरञ्चक्रपङ्कजम् //
29.m: in one of two cubits, it should measure one cubit, or he should proceed by increase through the door. / The lotus of the disc without a pedestal is square and without rays.

29.s:
padmārdhaṃ navabhiḥ proktaṃ nābhistu tisṛbhiḥ smṛtā /
aṣṭābhirdvārakān kuryānnemintu caturaṅgulaiḥ //
29.d:
पद्मार्धं नवभिः प्रोक्तं नाभिस्तु तिसृभिः स्मृता /
अष्टाभिर्द्वारकान् कुर्यान्नेमिन्तु चतुरङ्गुलैः //
29.m:
Half of the lotus is said to be nine [digits], and the nave is handed down as three;
one should make the door-openings eight [digits], and the rim four digits.

29.s:
tridhā(2) vibhajya ca kṣetramantardvābhyāmathāṅkayet /
pañcāntasvarasiddhyarthaṃ(3) teṣvasphālya likhedarān //
29.d:
त्रिधा(2) विभज्य च क्षेत्रमन्तर्द्वाभ्यामथाङ्कयेत् /
पञ्चान्तस्वरसिद्ध्यर्थं(3) तेष्वस्फाल्य लिखेदरान् //
29.m:
Dividing the field into three and then marking off within by two,
one should snap lines upon them to draw spokes for the sake of attaining the fifth interval.

29.s:
indīvaradalākārānathavā mātulāṅgavat /
padmapatrāyatānvāpi likhedicchānurūpataḥ //
29.d:
इन्दीवरदलाकारानथवा मातुलाङ्गवत् /
पद्मपत्रायतान्वापि लिखेदिच्छानुरूपतः //
29.m:
One should draw them shaped like blue lotus petals, or like the citron fruit,
or elongated like lotus petals, according to one's wish.

29.s:
bhrāmayitvā vahir nemāvarasandhyantare sthitaḥ /
bhrāmayedaramūlantu sandhimadhye vyavasthitaḥ //
:n
1 parimārjitā iti gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 dvidhā iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 pañcāntarastvasiddhyarthamiti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ pañcottarastu
siddhyarthamiti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 81
29.d:
भ्रामयित्वा वहिर् नेमावरसन्ध्यन्तरे स्थितः /
भ्रामयेदरमूलन्तु सन्धिमध्ये व्यवस्थितः //
:न्
1 परिमार्जिता इति घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 द्विधा इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 पञ्चान्तरस्त्वसिद्ध्यर्थमिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः पञ्चोत्तरस्तु
सिद्ध्यर्थमिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 81
29.m:
Rotating outside on the rim, positioned in the junction-interval of the spokes,
one should rotate the base of the spokes, situated in the midst of the junction.
:n
1 The reading in the manuscript marked gha is 'parimārjitā'.
2 The reading in the manuscript marked kha is 'dvidhā'.
3 The reading in the manuscript marked kha is 'pañcāntarastvasiddhyartham'; the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'pañcottarastu siddhyartham'.
:p 81

29.s:
aramadhye sthito madhamaraṇiṃ bhrāmayet samam /
evaṃ siddhyantarāḥ samyak mātulāṅganibhāḥ samāḥ //
29.d:
अरमध्ये स्थितो मधमरणिं भ्रामयेत् समम् /
एवं सिद्ध्यन्तराः सम्यक् मातुलाङ्गनिभाः समाः //
29.m:
Situated in the middle of a spoke, one should rotate the central turning-pin evenly;
thus the intervals are well produced, even, resembling citron fruits.

29.s:
vibhajya saptadhā kṣetraṃ caturdaśakaraṃ samam /
dvidhā kṛte śataṃ hy atra ṣaṇnavatyadhikāni tu //
29.d:
विभज्य सप्तधा क्षेत्रं चतुर्दशकरं समम् /
द्विधा कृते शतं ह्य् अत्र षण्नवत्यधिकानि तु //
29.m:
Dividing the field of fourteen cubits equally into seven parts,
when it is halved, there are indeed one hundred and ninety-six

29.s:
koṣṭakāni caturbhistair madhye bhadraṃ samālikhet /
parito visṛjedvīthyai tathā dikṣu samālikhet //
29.d:
कोष्टकानि चतुर्भिस्तैर् मध्ये भद्रं समालिखेत् /
परितो विसृजेद्वीथ्यै तथा दिक्षु समालिखेत् //
29.m:
squares; with four of them one should draw an auspicious figure in the centre.
One should leave space around for a pathway, and likewise in the directions one should draw

29.s:
kamalāni punarvīthyai paritaḥ parimṛjya tu /
dve dve madhyamakoṣṭhe tu grīvārthaṃ dikṣu lopayet //
29.d:
कमलानि पुनर्वीथ्यै परितः परिमृज्य तु /
द्वे द्वे मध्यमकोष्ठे तु ग्रीवार्थं दिक्षु लोपयेत् //
29.m:
lotuses; then, clearing around for a pathway,
one should erase two middle squares in each of the directions for the neck.

29.s:
catvāri vāhyataḥ paścāttrīṇi trīṇi tu lopayet /
grīvāpārśve vahistvekā śobhā sā parikīrtitā //
29.d:
चत्वारि वाह्यतः पश्चात्त्रीणि त्रीणि तु लोपयेत् /
ग्रीवापार्श्वे वहिस्त्वेका शोभा सा परिकीर्तिता //
29.m:
Then one should erase four on the outside, and three by three;
on the outside, beside the neck, is one [part]: that is proclaimed as the vestibule.

29.s:
vimṛjya vāhyakoṇeṣu saptāntastrīṇi mārjayet /
maṇḍalaṃ navabhāgaṃ syānnavavyūhaṃ hariṃ yajet //
29.d:
विमृज्य वाह्यकोणेषु सप्तान्तस्त्रीणि मार्जयेत् /
मण्डलं नवभागं स्यान्नवव्यूहं हरिं यजेत् //
29.m:
Erasing at the outer corners, one should wipe out three ending at the seventh.
The maṇḍala should consist of nine divisions; one should worship Hari in nine manifestations.

29.s:
pañcaviṃśatikavyūhaṃ maṇḍalaṃ viśvarūpagaṃ /
dvātriṃśaddhastakaṃ kṣetraṃ bhaktaṃ dvātriṃśatā samaṃ //
29.d:
पञ्चविंशतिकव्यूहं मण्डलं विश्वरूपगं /
द्वात्रिंशद्धस्तकं क्षेत्रं भक्तं द्वात्रिंशता समं //
29.m:
The maṇḍala of twenty-five manifestations pertains to the universal form;
a field measuring thirty-two cubits is divided equally into thirty-two.

29.s:
evaṃ kṛte caturviṃśatyadhikantu sahasrakaṃ /
koṣṭhakānāṃ samuddiṣṭaṃ madhye śoḍaśakoṣṭhakaiḥ //
29.d:
एवं कृते चतुर्विंशत्यधिकन्तु सहस्रकं /
कोष्ठकानां समुद्दिष्टं मध्ये शोडशकोष्ठकैः //
29.m:
When this is done, one thousand and twenty-four
squares are stated; with sixteen squares in the centre,

29.s:
bhadrakaṃ parilikhyātha pārśve paṅktiṃ vimṛjya tu /
tataḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ koṣṭair dikṣu bhadrāṣṭakaṃ likhet(1) //
29.d:
भद्रकं परिलिख्याथ पार्श्वे पङ्क्तिं विमृज्य तु /
ततः षोडशभिः कोष्टैर् दिक्षु भद्राष्टकं लिखेत्(1) //
29.m:
having drawn an auspicious figure and wiped out a row on the side,
one should then draw eight auspicious figures in the directions with sixteen squares [each].

29.s:
tatopi paṅktiṃ sammṛjya tadvat ṣoḍaśabhadrakaṃ /
likhitvā paritaḥ paṅktiṃ vimṛjyātha prakalpayet //
29.d:
ततोपि पङ्क्तिं सम्मृज्य तद्वत् षोडशभद्रकं /
लिखित्वा परितः पङ्क्तिं विमृज्याथ प्रकल्पयेत् //
29.m:
Then, having wiped out a row, one should likewise draw sixteen auspicious figures,
and having cleared a row all around, one should then arrange

29.s:
dvāradvādaśakaṃ dikṣu trīṇi trīṇi yathākramaṃ /
ṣaḍbhiḥ parilupyāntarmadhye catvāri pārśvayoḥ //
29.d:
द्वारद्वादशकं दिक्षु त्रीणि त्रीणि यथाक्रमं /
षड्भिः परिलुप्यान्तर्मध्ये चत्वारि पार्श्वयोः //
29.m:
twelve doorways in the directions, three by three in proper sequence;
erasing six on the inside, four in the middle, [and] on the flanks

29.s:
catvāryantarvahirdve tu śobhārthaṃ parimṛjya tu /
upadvārasiddhyarthaṃ trīṇyantaḥ pañca vāhyataḥ //
:n
1 dikṣu tatrāṣṭakaṃ likhediti kha, ga, gha,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 82
29.d:
चत्वार्यन्तर्वहिर्द्वे तु शोभार्थं परिमृज्य तु /
उपद्वारसिद्ध्यर्थं त्रीण्यन्तः पञ्च वाह्यतः //
:न्
1 दिक्षु तत्राष्टकं लिखेदिति ख, ग, घ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 82

29.s:
parimṛjya tathā śobhāṃ pūrvavat parikalpayet /
vahiḥ koṇeṣu saptāntastrīṇi koṣṭhāni mārjayet //
29.d:
परिमृज्य तथा शोभां पूर्ववत् परिकल्पयेत् /
वहिः कोणेषु सप्तान्तस्त्रीणि कोष्ठानि मार्जयेत् //
29.m:
and having wiped away, one should arrange the vestibule as before.
At the outer corners, one should wipe out three squares ending at the seventh.

29.s:
pañcaviṃśatikavyūhe paraṃ brahma yajet kaje(1) /
madhye pūrvāditaḥ padme vāsudevādayaḥ kramāt //
29.d:
पञ्चविंशतिकव्यूहे परं ब्रह्म यजेत् कजे(1) /
मध्ये पूर्वादितः पद्मे वासुदेवादयः क्रमात् //
29.m:
In the [maṇḍala] of twenty-five manifestations, one should worship the supreme Brahman on the lotus;
in the centre, on the lotus beginning from the east, Vāsudeva and the others in order.

29.s:
varāhaṃ pūjayitvā ca pūrvapadme tataḥ kramāt /
vyūhān sampūjayettāvat yāvat ṣaḍviṃśamo bhavet //
29.d:
वराहं पूजयित्वा च पूर्वपद्मे ततः क्रमात् /
व्यूहान् सम्पूजयेत्तावत् यावत् षड्विंशमो भवेत् //
29.m:
Having worshipped the Boar on the eastern lotus, one should then in sequence
worship the manifestations until there are twenty-six.

29.s:
yathoktaṃ vyūhamakhilamekasmin paṅkaje kramāt /
yaṣṭavyamiti yatnena(2) pracetā manyate 'dhvaraṃ(3) //
29.d:
यथोक्तं व्यूहमखिलमेकस्मिन् पङ्कजे क्रमात् /
यष्टव्यमिति यत्नेन(2) प्रचेता मन्यते ऽध्वरं(3) //
29.m:
The entire manifestation as prescribed should be worshipped sequentially on a single lotus;
Pracetas considers the sacrifice thus [performed] with care.

29.s:
satpantu mūrtibhedena vibhaktaṃ manyate 'cyutaṃ /
catvāriṃśat karaṃ kṣetraṃ hy uttaraṃ(4) vibhajet kramāt //
29.d:
सत्पन्तु मूर्तिभेदेन विभक्तं मन्यते ऽच्युतं /
चत्वारिंशत् करं क्षेत्रं ह्य् उत्तरं(4) विभजेत् क्रमात् //
29.m:
He considers Acyuta divided through distinct bodily forms.
A field of forty cubits should be divided progressively beyond:

29.s:
ekaikaṃ saptadhā bhūyastathaivaikaṃ dvidhā punaḥ /
catuḥṣaṣṭyuttaraṃ saptaśatānyekaṃ sahasrakaṃ //
29.d:
एकैकं सप्तधा भूयस्तथैवैकं द्विधा पुनः /
चतुःषष्ट्युत्तरं सप्तशतान्येकं सहस्रकं //
29.m:
each into seven again, and likewise each again into two,
[yielding] one thousand seven hundred and sixty-four

29.s:
koṣṭhakānāṃ bhadrakañca madhye ṣoḍaśakoṣṭhakaiḥ /
pārśve vīthīṃ tataścāṣṭabhadrāṇyatha ca vīthikā //
29.d:
कोष्ठकानां भद्रकञ्च मध्ये षोडशकोष्ठकैः /
पार्श्वे वीथीं ततश्चाष्टभद्राण्यथ च वीथिका //
29.m:
squares, and an auspicious figure in the centre with sixteen squares.
At the side a pathway, and then eight auspicious figures, and then a pathway,

29.s:
ṣoḍaśābjānyatho vīthī caturviṃśatipaṅkajaṃ /
vīthīpadmāni dvātriṃśat paṅktivīthikajānyatha //
29.d:
षोडशाब्जान्यथो वीथी चतुर्विंशतिपङ्कजं /
वीथीपद्मानि द्वात्रिंशत् पङ्क्तिवीथिकजान्यथ //
29.m:
sixteen lotuses, then a pathway, twenty-four lotuses,
a pathway, thirty-two lotuses, then lotuses of the pathway row,

29.s:
catvāriṃśattato vīthī śeṣapaṅktitrayeṇa ca /
dvāraśobhopaśobhāḥ syurdikṣu madhye vilopya ca //
29.d:
चत्वारिंशत्ततो वीथी शेषपङ्क्तित्रयेण च /
द्वारशोभोपशोभाः स्युर्दिक्षु मध्ये विलोप्य च //
29.m:
forty, and then a pathway; and by means of the remaining three rows
there should be doorways, vestibules, and minor vestibules, erasing in the directions and in the middle.

29.s:
dvicatuḥṣaḍdvārasiddhyai caturdikṣu vilopayet /
pañca trīṇyekakaṃ vāhye śobhopadvārasiddhaye //
:n
1 śubhe iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 yaṣṭavyamiti yajñena iti ga, gha, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
yaṣṭavyamiti mantreṇa iti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 pracetā manyate dhruvamiti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
4 hyuttamamiti ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 83
29.d:
द्विचतुःषड्द्वारसिद्ध्यै चतुर्दिक्षु विलोपयेत् /
पञ्च त्रीण्येककं वाह्ये शोभोपद्वारसिद्धये //
:न्
1 शुभे इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 यष्टव्यमिति यज्ञेन इति ग, घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
यष्टव्यमिति मन्त्रेण इति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 प्रचेता मन्यते ध्रुवमिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
4 ह्युत्तममिति ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 83
29.m:
For the attainment of two, four, and six doors, one should erase in the four directions;
[erasing] five, three, and one on the outside for the attainment of vestibules and secondary doorways.
:n
1 The reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'śubhe'.
2 The reading in the two manuscripts marked ga and gha is 'yaṣṭavyamiti yajñena'; the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'yaṣṭavyamiti mantreṇa'.
3 The reading in the manuscript marked kha is 'pracetā manyate dhruvam'.
4 The reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'hyuttamam'.
:p 83

29.s:
dvārāṇāṃ pārśvayorantaḥ ṣaḍ vā catvāri madhyataḥ /
dve dve lumpedevameva ṣaḍ bhavantyupaśobhikāḥ //
29.d:
द्वाराणां पार्श्वयोरन्तः षड् वा चत्वारि मध्यतः /
द्वे द्वे लुम्पेदेवमेव षड् भवन्त्युपशोभिकाः //
29.m:
On the flanks of the doorways, within, six, or four from the middle;
one should erase two by two; thus there are six minor vestibules.

29.s: ekasyāṃ diśi saṅkhyāḥ syuḥ catasraḥ prisaṅkhyayā //
29.d: एकस्यां दिशि सङ्ख्याः स्युः चतस्रः प्रिसङ्ख्यया //
29.m: In one direction the count should be four by enumeration.

29.s:
ekaikasyāṃ diśi trīṇi dvārāṇyapi bhavantyuta /
pañca pañca tu koṇeṣu paṅktau paṅktau kramāt mṛjet /
koṣṭakāni bhavedevaṃ martyeṣṭyaṃ maṇḍalaṃ śubhaṃ //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye maṇḍalādilakṣaṇaṃ nāma
ūnatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha triṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
maṇḍalavidhiḥ
29.d:
एकैकस्यां दिशि त्रीणि द्वाराण्यपि भवन्त्युत /
पञ्च पञ्च तु कोणेषु पङ्क्तौ पङ्क्तौ क्रमात् मृजेत् /
कोष्टकानि भवेदेवं मर्त्येष्ट्यं मण्डलं शुभं //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये मण्डलादिलक्षणं नाम
ऊनत्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ त्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
मण्डलविधिः
29.m:
In each single direction there are also three doorways.
One should erase five by five in the corners in row after row in succession;
thus there will be an auspicious maṇḍala pleasing to mortals.
Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter, entitled "Characteristics of the Maṇḍala and Related Matters," in the venerable Agni Mahāpurāṇa.
Now, the thirtieth chapter.
The Rule of the Maṇḍala.

30.s:
nārada uvāca
madhye padme yajedbrahma sāṅgaṃ pūrvebjanābhakaṃ /
āgneyebje ca prakṛtiṃ yāmyebje puruṣaṃ yajet //
30.d:
नारद उवाच
मध्ये पद्मे यजेद्ब्रह्म साङ्गं पूर्वेब्जनाभकं /
आग्नेयेब्जे च प्रकृतिं याम्येब्जे पुरुषं यजेत् //

30.s:
puruṣāddakṣiṇe ca vahniṃ nairṛte vāruṇenilaṃ /
ādityamaindave padme ṛgyajuś caiśapadmake //
30.d:
पुरुषाद्दक्षिणे च वह्निं नैरृते वारुणेनिलं /
आदित्यमैन्दवे पद्मे ऋग्यजुश् चैशपद्मके //
30.m:
And to the south of Puruṣa, Fire; in the south-west, Wind in the western [lotus];
the Sun in the northern lotus; and the Ṛg[veda] and Yajur[veda] in the north-eastern lotus.

30.s:
indrādīṃś ca dvitīyāyāṃ padme ṣoḍaśake tathā /
sāmātharvāṇamākāśaṃ vāyuṃ tejas tathā jalaṃ //
30.d:
इन्द्रादींश् च द्वितीयायां पद्मे षोडशके तथा /
सामाथर्वाणमाकाशं वायुं तेजस् तथा जलं //
30.m:
And Indra and the others in the second [circuit], likewise in the sixteen-petaled lotus:
the Sāma[veda], the Atharva[veda], space, air, fire, and water,

30.s:
pṛṭhivīñca manaś caiva śrotraṃ tvak cakṣurarcayet /
rasanāñca tathā ghrāṇaṃ bhūrbhuvaś caiva ṣoḍaśaṃ //
30.d:
पृठिवीञ्च मनश् चैव श्रोत्रं त्वक् चक्षुरर्चयेत् /
रसनाञ्च तथा घ्राणं भूर्भुवश् चैव षोडशं //
30.m:
earth, mind, hearing, skin, eye;
tongue, smell, and the sixteenth, Bhūḥ and Bhuvaḥ.

30.s:
maharjanastapaḥ satyaṃ tathāgniṣṭomameva ca /
atyagniṣṭomakaṃ(1) cokthaṃ ṣoḍaśīṃ vājapeyakaṃ //
30.d:
महर्जनस्तपः सत्यं तथाग्निष्टोममेव च /
अत्यग्निष्टोमकं(1) चोक्थं षोडशीं वाजपेयकं //
30.m:
Mahaḥ, Janaḥ, Tapaḥ, Satya, and also the Agniṣṭoma,
the Atyagniṣṭoma, the Uktha, the Ṣoḍaśin, the Vājapeya,

30.s:
atirātrañca sampūjya tathāptoryāmamarcayet /
mano buddhimahaṅkāraṃ śabdaṃ sparśañca rūpakaṃ //
30.d:
अतिरात्रञ्च सम्पूज्य तथाप्तोर्याममर्चयेत् /
मनो बुद्धिमहङ्कारं शब्दं स्पर्शञ्च रूपकं //
30.m:
and having worshipped the Atirātra, one should worship the Āptoryāma;
mind, intellect, ego, sound, touch, form,
taste, and smell in the twenty-four lotuses in due order;

29-r2.s:
:n
1 pratyagniṣṭomakamiti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ jyotiṣṭomakamiti
ṅa, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 84
jīvaṃ manodhipañcāhaṃ prakṛtiṃ śabdamātrakaṃ //
29-r2.d:
:न्
1 प्रत्यग्निष्टोमकमिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः ज्योतिष्टोमकमिति
ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 84
जीवं मनोधिपञ्चाहं प्रकृतिं शब्दमात्रकं //
29-r2.m:
:n
1 The reading in the manuscript marked kha is 'pratyagniṣṭomakam'; the reading in the manuscript marked ṅa is 'jyotiṣṭomakam'.
:p 84
the soul, the five lords of the mind, Prakṛti, and sound-subtle-element.

29-r2.s:
vāsudevādimūrtīñca tathā caiva daśatmakaṃ /
manaḥ śrotraṃ tvacaṃ prārcya cakṣuś ca rasanaṃ tathā //
29-r2.d:
वासुदेवादिमूर्तीञ्च तथा चैव दशत्मकं /
मनः श्रोत्रं त्वचं प्रार्च्य चक्षुश् च रसनं तथा //
29-r2.m:
and the forms of Vāsudeva and the rest, likewise consisting of ten principles,
having worshipped the mind, hearing, and touch, and likewise sight and taste,

29-r2.s:
ghrāṇaṃ vākpāṇipādañca dvātriṃśadvārijeṣvimān /
caturthāvaraṇe pūjyāḥ sāṅgāḥ saparivārakāḥ //
29-r2.d:
घ्राणं वाक्पाणिपादञ्च द्वात्रिंशद्वारिजेष्विमान् /
चतुर्थावरणे पूज्याः साङ्गाः सपरिवारकाः //
29-r2.m:
smell, speech, hands, and feet in these thirty-two lotuses.
In the fourth enclosure they are to be worshipped with their limbs and retinue.

29-r2.s:
pāyūpasthau ca sampūjya māsānāṃ dvādaśādhipān /
puruṣottamādiṣaḍviṃśān vāhyāvaraṇake yajet //
29-r2.d:
पायूपस्थौ च सम्पूज्य मासानां द्वादशाधिपान् /
पुरुषोत्तमादिषड्विंशान् वाह्यावरणके यजेत् //
29-r2.m:
Having worshipped the anus and genitals, and the twelve lords of the months,
one should worship the twenty-six beginning with Puruṣottama in the outer enclosure.

29-r2.s:
cakrābje teṣu sampūjyā māsānāṃ patayaḥ kramāt /
aṣṭau prakṛtayaḥ ṣaḍvā pañcātha caturo 'pare //
29-r2.d:
चक्राब्जे तेषु सम्पूज्या मासानां पतयः क्रमात् /
अष्टौ प्रकृतयः षड्वा पञ्चाथ चतुरो ऽपरे //
29-r2.m:
In the lotus-wheel, the lords of the months should be worshipped in them in order.
The primary constituents are eight, or six, or five, or others say four.

29-r2.s:
rajaḥ pātaṃ tataḥ kuryāllikhite maṇḍale śṛṇu /
karṇikā pītavarṇā syādrekhāḥ sarvāḥ sitāḥ samāḥ //
29-r2.d:
रजः पातं ततः कुर्याल्लिखिते मण्डले शृणु /
कर्णिका पीतवर्णा स्याद्रेखाः सर्वाः सिताः समाः //
29-r2.m:
Hear then how to sprinkle the powder when the maṇḍala is drawn:
the pericarp should be yellow; all the lines should be white and even;

29-r2.s:
dvihaste 'ṅguṣṭamātrāḥ syurhaste cārdhasamāḥ sitāḥ /
padmaṃ śuklena sandhīṃstu kṛṣṇena śyāmatothavā //
29-r2.d:
द्विहस्ते ऽङ्गुष्टमात्राः स्युर्हस्ते चार्धसमाः सिताः /
पद्मं शुक्लेन सन्धींस्तु कृष्णेन श्यामतोथवा //
29-r2.m:
in a two-cubit [diagram] they should measure a thumb['s breadth]; in a one-cubit [diagram] they should be half that, and white.
[One should fill] the lotus with white, but the joints with black or dark green;

29-r2.s:
keśarā raktapītāḥ syuḥ koṇān raktena pūrayet /
bhūṣayedyogapīṭhantu yatheṣṭaṃ sārvavarṇikaiḥ //
29-r2.d:
केशरा रक्तपीताः स्युः कोणान् रक्तेन पूरयेत् /
भूषयेद्योगपीठन्तु यथेष्टं सार्ववर्णिकैः //
29-r2.m:
the filaments should be red and yellow; one should fill the corners with red.
One should decorate the yoga-seat as one wishes with all colors.

29-r2.s:
latāvitānapatrādyair vīthikāmupaśobhayet /
pīṭhadvāre tu śuklena śobhāraktena pītataḥ //
29-r2.d:
लतावितानपत्राद्यैर् वीथिकामुपशोभयेत् /
पीठद्वारे तु शुक्लेन शोभारक्तेन पीततः //
29-r2.m:
One should adorn the pathway with creepers, canopies, leaves, and the like.
At the doorway of the seat, with white; the decorative border with red [and] yellow;

29-r2.s:
upaśobhāñca nīlena koṇaśaṅkhyāṃś ca vai sitān /
bhadrake pūraṇaṃ proktamevamanyeṣu pūraṇaṃ //
29-r2.d:
उपशोभाञ्च नीलेन कोणशङ्ख्यांश् च वै सितान् /
भद्रके पूरणं प्रोक्तमेवमन्येषु पूरणं //
29-r2.m:
the secondary border with blue; and the corner conches with white.
Filling has been described in the bhadraka [design]; thus is the filling in others.

29-r2.s:
trikoṇaṃ sitaraktena kṛṣṇena ca vibhūṣayet /
dvikoṇaṃ raktapītābhyāṃ nābhiṃ kṛṣṇena cakrake //
29-r2.d:
त्रिकोणं सितरक्तेन कृष्णेन च विभूषयेत् /
द्विकोणं रक्तपीताभ्यां नाभिं कृष्णेन चक्रके //
29-r2.m:
One should decorate a triangle with white, red, and black;
a two-cornered [figure] with red and yellow; the navel with black in a wheel;

29-r2.s:
arakān pītaraktābhiḥ śyāmān nemintu raktataḥ /
sitaśyāmāruṇāḥ kṛṣṇāḥ pītā rekhāstu vāhyataḥ //
29-r2.d:
अरकान् पीतरक्ताभिः श्यामान् नेमिन्तु रक्ततः /
सितश्यामारुणाः कृष्णाः पीता रेखास्तु वाह्यतः //
29-r2.m:
the spokes with yellow and red; the dark-green rim with red.
White, dark green, red, black, and yellow lines are on the outside.

29-r2.s:
śālipiṣṭādi śuklaṃ syādraktaṃ kausumbhakādikam /
haridrayā ca hāridraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ syāddagdhadhānyataḥ //
:p 85
29-r2.d:
शालिपिष्टादि शुक्लं स्याद्रक्तं कौसुम्भकादिकम् /
हरिद्रया च हारिद्रं कृष्णं स्याद्दग्धधान्यतः //
:प् 85

29-r2.s:
śamīpatrādikaiḥ śyāmaṃ vījānāṃ lakṣajāpyataḥ /
caturlakṣaistu mantrāṇāṃ vidyānāṃ lakṣasādhanam //
29-r2.d:
शमीपत्रादिकैः श्यामं वीजानां लक्षजाप्यतः /
चतुर्लक्षैस्तु मन्त्राणां विद्यानां लक्षसाधनम् //
29-r2.m:
dark green with śamī leaves and the like. By reciting one hundred thousand seed-syllables,
with four hundred thousand of mantras, [and] with one hundred thousand the attainment of the vidyās [is achieved].

29-r2.s:
ayutaṃ buddhividyānāṃ stotrāṇāñca sahasrakam /
pūrvamevātha lakṣeṇa mantraśuddhis tathātmanaḥ //
29-r2.d:
अयुतं बुद्धिविद्यानां स्तोत्राणाञ्च सहस्रकम् /
पूर्वमेवाथ लक्षेण मन्त्रशुद्धिस् तथात्मनः //
29-r2.m:
Ten thousand of the buddhi-vidyās, and a thousand of the hymns of praise.
First, by a hundred thousand [recitations], purification of the mantra and of oneself [is achieved];

29-r2.s:
tathāpareṇa lakṣeṇa mantraḥ kṣetrīkṛto bhavet /
pūrvamevāsamo homo vījānāṃ samprakīrtitaḥ //
29-r2.d:
तथापरेण लक्षेण मन्त्रः क्षेत्रीकृतो भवेत् /
पूर्वमेवासमो होमो वीजानां सम्प्रकीर्तितः //
29-r2.m:
then, by another hundred thousand, the mantra becomes cultivated.
Preliminary unmatched fire oblation of the seed-syllables has been declared.

29-r2.s:
pūrvasevā daśāṃśena mantrādīnāṃ prakīrtitā /
paraś carye tu mantre tu māsikaṃ vratamācaret //
29-r2.d:
पूर्वसेवा दशांशेन मन्त्रादीनां प्रकीर्तिता /
परश् चर्ये तु मन्त्रे तु मासिकं व्रतमाचरेत् //
29-r2.m:
Preliminary service of mantras and the rest is declared to be by a tenth part.
When a mantra is to be practiced further, one should perform a month-long votive observance:

29-r2.s:
bhuvi nyasedvāmapādaṃ na gṛhṇīyāt pratigraham /
evaṃ dvitriguṇenaiva madhyamottamasiddhayaḥ //
29-r2.d:
भुवि न्यसेद्वामपादं न गृह्णीयात् प्रतिग्रहम् /
एवं द्वित्रिगुणेनैव मध्यमोत्तमसिद्धयः //
29-r2.m:
one should place the left foot on the earth and not accept a gift.
Thus, by doubling or tripling [the practice], middling and highest attainments [are achieved].

29-r2.s:
mantradhyānaṃ pravakṣyāmi yena syānmantrajaṃ phalam /
sthūlaṃ śabdamayaṃ rūpaṃ vigrahaṃ vāhyamiṣyate //
29-r2.d:
मन्त्रध्यानं प्रवक्ष्यामि येन स्यान्मन्त्रजं फलम् /
स्थूलं शब्दमयं रूपं विग्रहं वाह्यमिष्यते //
29-r2.m:
I shall declare the meditation on mantras by which the fruit born of the mantra arises.
The gross form consists of sound; the external image is prescribed [as such].

29-r2.s:
sukṣmāṃ jyotirmayaṃ rūpaṃ hārdaṃ cintāmayaṃ bhavet /
cintayā rahitaṃ yattu tat paraṃ prakīrtitam //
29-r2.d:
सुक्ष्मां ज्योतिर्मयं रूपं हार्दं चिन्तामयं भवेत् /
चिन्तया रहितं यत्तु तत् परं प्रकीर्तितम् //
29-r2.m:
The subtle form consists of light; the mental [form] in the heart consists of thought.
That which is devoid of thought is proclaimed as the supreme.

29-r2.s:
varāhasiṃhaśaktīnāṃ sthūlarūpaṃ pradhānataḥ /
cintayā rahitaṃ rūpaṃ vāsudevasya kīrtitam //
29-r2.d:
वराहसिंहशक्तीनां स्थूलरूपं प्रधानतः /
चिन्तया रहितं रूपं वासुदेवस्य कीर्तितम् //
29-r2.m:
The form of the Boar, the Lion, and the Śaktis is primarily gross.
The form devoid of thought is declared to be that of Vāsudeva.

29-r2.s:
itareṣāṃ smṛtaṃ rūpaṃ hārdaṃ cintāmayaṃ sadā /
sthūlaṃ vairājamākhyātaṃ sūkṣmaṃ vai liṅgitaṃ bhavet //
29-r2.d:
इतरेषां स्मृतं रूपं हार्दं चिन्तामयं सदा /
स्थूलं वैराजमाख्यातं सूक्ष्मं वै लिङ्गितं भवेत् //
29-r2.m:
The form of the others is traditionally regarded as being in the heart, consisting always of thought.
The gross is called universal; the subtle is indeed characterized [by the linga-śarīra].

29-r2.s:
cintayā rahitaṃ rūpamaiśvaraṃ parikīrtitam /
hṛtpuṇḍarīkanilayañcaitanyaṃ jyotiravyayam //
29-r2.d:
चिन्तया रहितं रूपमैश्वरं परिकीर्तितम् /
हृत्पुण्डरीकनिलयञ्चैतन्यं ज्योतिरव्ययम् //
29-r2.m:
The form devoid of thought is declared to be divine:
abiding in the lotus of the heart, consciousness, imperishable light.

29-r2.s:
vījaṃ vījātmakaṃ dhyāyet kadambakusumākṛtiṃ /
kumbhāntaragato dīpo niruddhaprasavo yathā //
29-r2.d:
वीजं वीजात्मकं ध्यायेत् कदम्बकुसुमाकृतिं /
कुम्भान्तरगतो दीपो निरुद्धप्रसवो यथा //
29-r2.m:
One should meditate on the seed-syllable whose nature is the source, having the form of a kadamba blossom.
Just as a lamp inside a pot, its spread obstructed,

29-r2.s:
saṃhataḥ kevalastiṣṭhedevaṃ mantreśvaro hṛdi /
anekaśuṣire kumbhe tāvanmātrā gabhastayaḥ //
29-r2.d:
संहतः केवलस्तिष्ठेदेवं मन्त्रेश्वरो हृदि /
अनेकशुषिरे कुम्भे तावन्मात्रा गभस्तयः //
29-r2.m:
stands concentrated and alone, so does the lord of the mantra stand in the heart.
Just as through a pot with many holes rays radiate out

29-r2.s:
prasaranti vahistadvannāḍībhirvījaraśmayaḥ /
:p 86
athāvabhāsato daivīmātmīkṛtya tanuṃ sthitāḥ //
29-r2.d:
प्रसरन्ति वहिस्तद्वन्नाडीभिर्वीजरश्मयः /
:प् 86
अथावभासतो दैवीमात्मीकृत्य तनुं स्थिताः //

29-r2.s:
hṛdayāt prasthitā nāḍyo darśanendriyagocarāḥ /
agnīṣomātmake tāsāṃ nāḍyau nāsāgrasaṃsthite //
29-r2.d:
हृदयात् प्रस्थिता नाड्यो दर्शनेन्द्रियगोचराः /
अग्नीषोमात्मके तासां नाड्यौ नासाग्रसंस्थिते //
29-r2.m:
the channels issuing from the heart are the realm of the sensory faculties.
Among them, two channels partaking of Fire and Soma reside at the tip of the nose.

29-r2.s:
samyagguhyena yogena jitvā dehasamīraṇam /
japadhyānarato mantrī mantralakṣaṇamaśnute(1) //
29-r2.d:
सम्यग्गुह्येन योगेन जित्वा देहसमीरणम् /
जपध्यानरतो मन्त्री मन्त्रलक्षणमश्नुते(1) //
29-r2.m:
Having thoroughly conquered the bodily breath through esoteric yoga,
the mantra practitioner, devoted to recitation and meditation, attains the characteristics of the mantra.

29-r2.s:
saṃśuddhabhūtatanmātraḥ sakāmo yogamabhyasan /
aṇimādimavāpnoti viraktaḥ pravilaṅghya ca /
devātmake bhūtamātrānmucyate cendriyagrahāt //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye maṇḍalādivarṇanaṃ nāma triṃśo
'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha ekatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
mārjanavidhānaṃ
29-r2.d:
संशुद्धभूततन्मात्रः सकामो योगमभ्यसन् /
अणिमादिमवाप्नोति विरक्तः प्रविलङ्घ्य च /
देवात्मके भूतमात्रान्मुच्यते चेन्द्रियग्रहात् //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये मण्डलादिवर्णनं नाम त्रिंशो
ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ एकत्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
मार्जनविधानं
29-r2.m:
Having purified the gross elements and subtle elements, practicing yoga with desire,
he obtains atom-sized minimization and the other [perfections]; and transcending them, detached,
in the divine nature he is freed from the elements and from the grasp of the senses.
:e Thus ends the thirtieth chapter, titled Description of the Maṇḍala and Others, in the venerable early Mahāpurāṇa, the Āgneya.
:ś Now the thirty-first chapter.
The Rite of Sprinkling.

31.s:
agnir uvāca
rakṣāṃ svasya pareṣāñca vakṣye tāṃ mārjanāhvayāṃ /
yayā vimucyate duḥkhaiḥ sukhañca prāpnuyānnaraḥ(2) //
31.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
रक्षां स्वस्य परेषाञ्च वक्ष्ये तां मार्जनाह्वयां /
यया विमुच्यते दुःखैः सुखञ्च प्राप्नुयान्नरः(2) //
31.m:
Agni said:
I shall explain the protective rite for oneself and others, known as the ritual cleansing,
by which a man is freed from miseries and attains happiness.

31.s:
oṃ namaḥ paramārthāya puruṣāya mahātmane /
arūpabahurūpāya vyāpine paramātmane //
31.d:
ओं नमः परमार्थाय पुरुषाय महात्मने /
अरूपबहुरूपाय व्यापिने परमात्मने //
31.m:
Om, reverence to the supreme reality, the Person, the Great Soul,
the formless one who has many forms, the all-pervasive Supreme Self.

31.s:
niṣkalmaṣāya śuddhāya dhyānayogaratāya ca /
namaskṛtya pravakṣyāmi yat tatsidhyatu me vacaḥ //
31.d:
निष्कल्मषाय शुद्धाय ध्यानयोगरताय च /
नमस्कृत्य प्रवक्ष्यामि यत् तत्सिध्यतु मे वचः //
31.m:
To the stainless, the pure, and the one delighting in the yoga of meditation,
having bowed, I shall speak; may that speech of mine be effective.

31.s:
varāhāya nṛsiṃhāya vāmanāya mahāmune /
namaskṛtya pravakṣyāmi yattatsidhyatu me vacaḥ //
:n
1 mantrajaṃ phalamaśnute iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 sukhaṃ brahmāpnuyānnaraḥ iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 87
31.d:
वराहाय नृसिंहाय वामनाय महामुने /
नमस्कृत्य प्रवक्ष्यामि यत्तत्सिध्यतु मे वचः //
:न्
1 मन्त्रजं फलमश्नुते इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 सुखं ब्रह्माप्नुयान्नरः इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 87
31.m:
To the Boar, to Nṛsiṃha, to Vāmana, O great sage,
having bowed, I shall speak; may that speech of mine be effective.
[Footnote]
[Variant] “He enjoys the fruit born of the mantra” is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
[Variant] “A man attains the happiness of Brahman” is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.

31.s:
trivikramāya rāmāya vaikuṇṭhāya narāya ca /
namaskṛtya pravakṣyāmi yattat sidhyatu me vacaḥ //
31.d:
त्रिविक्रमाय रामाय वैकुण्ठाय नराय च /
नमस्कृत्य प्रवक्ष्यामि यत्तत् सिध्यतु मे वचः //
31.m:
To Trivikrama, to Rāma, to Vaikuṇṭha, and to Nara,
having bowed, I shall speak; may that speech of mine be effective.

31.s:
varāha narasiṃheśa vāmaneśa trivikrama /
haragrīveśa sarveśa hṛṣīkeśa harāśubham //
31.d:
वराह नरसिंहेश वामनेश त्रिविक्रम /
हरग्रीवेश सर्वेश हृषीकेश हराशुभम् //
31.m:
O Boar, O Lord Narasiṃha, O Lord Vāmana, O Trivikrama,
O Lord Hayagrīva, O Lord of all, O Hṛṣīkeśa, remove misfortune!

31.s:
aparājitacakrādyaiś caturbhiḥ paramāyudhaiḥ /
akhaṇḍitānubhāvaistvaṃ(1) sarvaduṣṭaharo bhava //
31.d:
अपराजितचक्राद्यैश् चतुर्भिः परमायुधैः /
अखण्डितानुभावैस्त्वं(1) सर्वदुष्टहरो भव //
31.m:
With the four supreme weapons, beginning with the invincible discus,
endowed with unbroken power, be the destroyer of all wicked forces!

31.s:
harāmukasya duritaṃ sarvañca kuśalaṃ kuru /
mṛtyubandhārtabhayadaṃ duritasya ca yat phalam //
31.d:
हरामुकस्य दुरितं सर्वञ्च कुशलं कुरु /
मृत्युबन्धार्तभयदं दुरितस्य च यत् फलम् //
31.m:
Remove the wickedness from so-and-so and bring about all auspiciousness,
as well as whatever fruit of wickedness causes death, bondage, distress, and fear.

31.s:
parābhidhyānasahitaiḥ prayuktañcābhicārakam /
gadasparśamahārogaprayogaṃ jarayā jara //
31.d:
पराभिध्यानसहितैः प्रयुक्तञ्चाभिचारकम् /
गदस्पर्शमहारोगप्रयोगं जरया जर //
31.m:
Wear down through decay malevolent sorcery cast together with ill-will from others,
[and] the application of severe illnesses through the contact of diseases!

31.s:
oṃ namo vāsudevāya namaḥ kṛṣṇāya khaḍgine /
namaḥ puṣkaranetrāya keśavāyādicakriṇe //
31.d:
ओं नमो वासुदेवाय नमः कृष्णाय खड्गिने /
नमः पुष्करनेत्राय केशवायादिचक्रिणे //
31.m:
Om, reverence to Vāsudeva; reverence to Kṛṣṇa, wielder of the sword;
reverence to the lotus-eyed Keśava, the primeval discus-bearer!

31.s:
namaḥ kamalakiñjalkapītanirmalavāsase /
mahāhararipuskandhasṛṣṭacakrāya cakriṇe //
31.d:
नमः कमलकिञ्जल्कपीतनिर्मलवाससे /
महाहररिपुस्कन्धसृष्टचक्राय चक्रिणे //
31.m:
Reverence to the one whose pure garments are yellow like lotus filaments,
the discus-wielder who hurled the discus at the neck of the great enemy of Hara!

31.s:
dṃṣṭroddhṛtakṣitibhṛte(2) trayīmūrtimate namaḥ /
mahāyajñavarāhāya śeṣabhogāṅkaśāyine //
31.d:
द्ंष्ट्रोद्धृतक्षितिभृते(2) त्रयीमूर्तिमते नमः /
महायज्ञवराहाय शेषभोगाङ्कशायिने //
31.m:
Reverence to the bearer of the three Vedas in bodily form, who raised the earth upon his tusk,
to the Boar of the great sacrifice, who reclines on the coils of Śeṣa!

31.s:
taptahāṭakakeśāgrajvalatpāvakalocana /
vajrādhikanakhasparśaṃ divyasiṃha namostu te //
31.d:
तप्तहाटककेशाग्रज्वलत्पावकलोचन /
वज्राधिकनखस्पर्शं दिव्यसिंह नमोस्तु ते //
31.m:
O you whose hair-tips are like molten gold, whose eyes are blazing fires,
whose claw-touch surpasses the thunderbolt, divine Lion, reverence to you!

31.s:
kāśyapāyātihrasvāya ṛgyajuḥsāmabhūṣita /
tubhyaṃ vāmanarūpāyākramate gāṃ(3) namo namaḥ //
31.d:
काश्यपायातिह्रस्वाय ऋग्यजुःसामभूषित /
तुभ्यं वामनरूपायाक्रमते गां(3) नमो नमः //
31.m:
To the son of Kaśyapa, exceedingly diminutive, adorned with Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma,
to you in the form of Vāmana who stride across the earth, reverence, reverence!

31.s:
varāhāśeṣaduṣṭāni sarvapāpaphalāni vai /
marda marda mahādaṃṣṭra marda marda ca tatphalam //
:n
1 akhaṇḍitātmabhāvaistvamiti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 daṃṣṭroddhṛtabhūmibhartre iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 sṛjate gāmiti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 88
31.d:
वराहाशेषदुष्टानि सर्वपापफलानि वै /
मर्द मर्द महादंष्ट्र मर्द मर्द च तत्फलम् //
:न्
1 अखण्डितात्मभावैस्त्वमिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 दंष्ट्रोद्धृतभूमिभर्त्रे इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 सृजते गामिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 88
31.m:
O Boar, crush, crush, O great-tusked one, crush, crush all wicked things,
all fruits of sin, and the consequences thereof!
[Footnote]
[Variant] “with unbroken self-nature, you” is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
[Variant] “to the supporter of the earth raised on the tusk” is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
[Variant] “who emits the earth” is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.

31.s:
narasiṃha karālākhya dantaprāntānalojjvala /
bhañja bhañja ninādena duṣṭānyasyārtināśana //
31.d:
नरसिंह करालाख्य दन्तप्रान्तानलोज्ज्वल /
