भञ्ज भञ्ज निनादेन दुष्टान्यस्यार्तिनाशन //
31.m:
O Narasiṃha, named the Terrifying One, radiant with fire at the tips of your teeth,
break, break with your roar the wicked afflictions of this person, O destroyer of distress!

31.s:
ṛgyajuḥsāmagarbhābhirvāgbhirvāmanarūpadhṛk /
praśamaṃ sarvaduḥkhāni nayattvasya janārdanaḥ //
31.d:
ऋग्यजुःसामगर्भाभिर्वाग्भिर्वामनरूपधृक् /
प्रशमं सर्वदुःखानि नयत्त्वस्य जनार्दनः //
31.m:
Assuming the form of Vāmana, with words embodying the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman,
may Janārdana bring all the miseries of this person to cessation!

31.s:
aikāhikaṃ dvyāhikañca tathā tridivasaṃ jvaram /
cāturthakantathātyugrantathaiva satatajvaram //
31.d:
ऐकाहिकं द्व्याहिकञ्च तथा त्रिदिवसं ज्वरम् /
चातुर्थकन्तथात्युग्रन्तथैव सततज्वरम् //
31.m:
Fever recurring every day, every second day, or every third day,
as well as the extremely violent quartan fever, and continuous fever,

31.s:
doṣotthaṃ sannipātotthaṃ tathaivāgantukaṃ jvaram /
śamaṃ nayāśu govinda cchindhi cchindhyasya vedanām(1) //
31.d:
दोषोत्थं सन्निपातोत्थं तथैवागन्तुकं ज्वरम् /
शमं नयाशु गोविन्द च्छिन्धि च्छिन्ध्यस्य वेदनाम्(1) //
31.m:
fever born of humoral disturbance, born of combined humours, and also accidental fever—
bring them swiftly to peace, O Govinda; sever, sever his pain!

31.s:
netraduḥkhaṃ śiroduḥkhaṃ duḥkhañcodarasambhavam /
antaḥśvāsamatiśvāsaṃ(2) paritāpaṃ savepathum //
31.d:
नेत्रदुःखं शिरोदुःखं दुःखञ्चोदरसम्भवम् /
अन्तःश्वासमतिश्वासं(2) परितापं सवेपथुम् //
31.m:
Eye affliction, head affliction, affliction originating in the abdomen,
shortness of breath, excessive breathing, burning heat accompanied by trembling,

31.s:
gudaghrāṇāṅghrirogāṃś ca kuṣṭharogāṃs tathā kṣayaṃ(3) /
kāmalādīṃs tathā rogān pramehāṃścātidāruṇān //
31.d:
गुदघ्राणाङ्घ्रिरोगांश् च कुष्ठरोगांस् तथा क्षयं(3) /
कामलादींस् तथा रोगान् प्रमेहांश्चातिदारुणान् //
31.m:
diseases of the anus, nose, and feet, leprosy, consumption,
jaundice and other diseases, and exceedingly dreadful urinary disorders,

31.s:
bhagandarātisārāṃś ca mukharogāṃś ca valgulīm /
aśmarīṃ mūtrakṛcchrāṃś ca rogānanyāṃś ca dāruṇān //
31.d:
भगन्दरातिसारांश् च मुखरोगांश् च वल्गुलीम् /
अश्मरीं मूत्रकृच्छ्रांश् च रोगानन्यांश् च दारुणान् //
31.m:
fistula-in-ano, dysentery, mouth diseases, valgulī-disease,
urinary calculus, strangury, and other terrible diseases—

31.s:
ye vātaprabhavā rogā ye ca pittasamudbhavāḥ /
kaphodbhavāś ca ye kecit ye cānye sānnipātikāḥ //
31.d:
ये वातप्रभवा रोगा ये च पित्तसमुद्भवाः /
कफोद्भवाश् च ये केचित् ये चान्ये सान्निपातिकाः //
31.m:
those diseases that originate from wind, those that arise from bile,
whatever arise from phlegm, and those others born of combined humours,

31.s:
āgantukāś ca ye rogā lūtā visphoṭakādayaḥ /
te sarve praśamaṃ yāntu vāsudevāpamārjitāḥ(5) //
31.d:
आगन्तुकाश् च ये रोगा लूता विस्फोटकादयः /
ते सर्वे प्रशमं यान्तु वासुदेवापमार्जिताः(5) //
31.m:
and exogenous diseases such as spider poison, boils, and the like—
may all of them go to pacification, cleansed away by Vāsudeva!

31.s:
vilayaṃ yāntu te sarve viṣṇoruccāraṇena ca /
kṣayaṃ gachhantu cāśeṣāste cakrābhihatā hareḥ //
:n
1 chinda chindāsya vedanāmiti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 aniśvāsamatiśvāsamiti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 tathaiva ca iti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
4 ye rogāḥ pittasambhavā iti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
5 vāsudevaparājitā iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 89
31.d:
विलयं यान्तु ते सर्वे विष्णोरुच्चारणेन च /
क्षयं गछ्हन्तु चाशेषास्ते चक्राभिहता हरेः //
:न्
1 छिन्द छिन्दास्य वेदनामिति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 अनिश्वासमतिश्वासमिति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 तथैव च इति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
4 ये रोगाः पित्तसम्भवा इति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
5 वासुदेवपराजिता इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 89
31.m:
May they all dissolve away through the utterance of Viṣṇu's name;
and may they completely perish, struck by the discus of Hari!
[Footnote]
[Variant] “sever, sever his pain” is the reading in the manuscript marked ga.
[Variant] “breathlessness and excessive breathing” is the reading in the manuscript marked ga.
[Variant] “and likewise” is the reading in the manuscript marked ga.
[Variant] “the diseases that arise from bile” is the reading in the manuscript marked ga.
[Variant] “vanquished by Vāsudeva” is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.

31.s:
acyutānantagovindanāmoccāraṇabhīṣitāḥ /
naśyanti sakalā rogāḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmyaham //
31.d:
अच्युतानन्तगोविन्दनामोच्चारणभीषिताः /
नश्यन्ति सकला रोगाः सत्यं सत्यं वदाम्यहम् //
31.m:
Terrified by the utterance of the names Acyuta, Ananta, and Govinda,
all diseases perish; truly, truly do I say this.

31.s:
sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ vāpi kṛtrimaṃ cāpi yadviṣam /
dantodbhavaṃ nakhabhavamākāśaprabhavaṃ viṣam //
31.d:
स्थावरं जङ्गमं वापि कृत्रिमं चापि यद्विषम् /
दन्तोद्भवं नखभवमाकाशप्रभवं विषम् //
31.m:
Poison that is inanimate or animate, or also that which is artificial,
poison arising from fangs, arising from claws, or arising from the sky,

31.s:
lūtādiprabhavaṃ yacca viṣamanyattu duḥkhadaṃ /
śamaṃ nayatu tat sarvaṃ kīrtitosya janārdanaḥ //
31.d:
लूतादिप्रभवं यच्च विषमन्यत्तु दुःखदं /
शमं नयतु तत् सर्वं कीर्तितोस्य जनार्दनः //
31.m:
and whatever poison originates from spiders and the like, or any other that causes misery—
may Janārdana, being praised, bring all of that to cessation for him!

31.s:
grahān pretagrahāṃścāpi tathā vai ḍākinīgrahān(1) /
vetālāṃś ca piśācāṃś ca gandharvān yakṣarākṣasān(2) //
31.d:
ग्रहान् प्रेतग्रहांश्चापि तथा वै डाकिनीग्रहान्(1) /
वेतालांश् च पिशाचांश् च गन्धर्वान् यक्षराक्षसान्(2) //
31.m:
Seizing spirits, spirits of the dead, and also ḍākinī spirits,
vetālas, piśācas, gandharvas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas,

31.s:
śakunīpūtanādyāṃś ca tathā vaināyakān grahān /
mukhamaṇḍīṃ tathā krūrāṃ revatīṃ vṛddharevatīm //
31.d:
शकुनीपूतनाद्यांश् च तथा वैनायकान् ग्रहान् /
मुखमण्डीं तथा क्रूरां रेवतीं वृद्धरेवतीम् //
31.m:
the seizing spirits beginning with Śakunī and Pūtanā, and the seizing spirits of Vināyaka,
Mukhamaṇḍī, the cruel Revatī, and Vṛddharevatī,

31.s:
vṛddhakākhyān grahāṃścogrāṃs tathā mātṛgrahānapi /
bālasya viṣṇoś caritaṃ hantu bālagrahānimān //
31.d:
वृद्धकाख्यान् ग्रहांश्चोग्रांस् तथा मातृग्रहानपि /
बालस्य विष्णोश् चरितं हन्तु बालग्रहानिमान् //
31.m:
the fierce seizing spirits called Vṛddhaka, and also the mother spirits—
may the deeds of child Viṣṇu slay these child-afflicting spirits!

31.s:
vṛddhāś ca ye grahāḥ kecidye ca bālagrahāḥ kvacit /
narasiṃhasya te dṛṣṭyā dagdhā ye cāpi yauvane //
31.d:
वृद्धाश् च ये ग्रहाः केचिद्ये च बालग्रहाः क्वचित् /
नरसिंहस्य ते दृष्ट्या दग्धा ये चापि यौवने //
31.m:
And whatever spirits afflict the aged, and whatever spirits afflict children anywhere,
and also those in youth, are burned by the glance of Narasiṃha.

31.s:
sadā(3) karālavadano narasiṃho mahābalaḥ /
grahānaśeṣānniḥśeṣān karotu jagato hitaḥ //
31.d:
सदा(3) करालवदनो नरसिंहो महाबलः /
ग्रहानशेषान्निःशेषान् करोतु जगतो हितः //
31.m:
May the terrifying-faced Narasiṃha of great power, who works the welfare of the world,
wholly eliminate all seizing spirits without remainder!

31.s:
narasiṃha mahāsiṃha jvālāmālojjvalānana /
grahānaśeṣān sarveśa khāda khādāgnilocana //
31.d:
नरसिंह महासिंह ज्वालामालोज्ज्वलानन /
ग्रहानशेषान् सर्वेश खाद खादाग्निलोचन //
31.m:
O Narasiṃha, great Lion, whose face is ablaze with garlands of flames,
O fire-eyed Lord of all, devour, devour all seizing spirits!

31.s:
ye rogā ye mahotpātā yadviṣaṃ ye mahāgrahāḥ /
yāni ca krūrabhṛtāni grahapīḍāś ca dāruṇāḥ //
31.d:
ये रोगा ये महोत्पाता यद्विषं ये महाग्रहाः /
यानि च क्रूरभृतानि ग्रहपीडाश् च दारुणाः //
31.m:
Whatever diseases, whatever great portents, whatever poison, whatever great seizing spirits,
and whatever cruel beings and dreadful afflictions of planets there are,

31.s:
śastrakṣateṣu ye doṣā jvālāgardabhakādayaḥ /
tāni sarvāṇi sarvātmā paramātmā janārdanaḥ //
:n
1 tathā vetālikān grahāniti gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 gandharvān rāksasānapi iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 śaṭā iti kha, ṅa, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
:p 90
31.d:
शस्त्रक्षतेषु ये दोषा ज्वालागर्दभकादयः /
तानि सर्वाणि सर्वात्मा परमात्मा जनार्दनः //
:न्
1 तथा वेतालिकान् ग्रहानिति घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 गन्धर्वान् राक्ससानपि इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 शटा इति ख, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
:प् 90
31.m:
whatever disorders arise in weapon-wounds, such as erysipelas and the like—
all those, Janārdana, the Self of all, the Supreme Self,
[Footnote]
[Variant] “and likewise the vetālika seizing spirits” is the reading in the manuscript marked gha.
[Variant] “gandharvas and rākṣasas as well” is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
[Variant] “with manes” is the reading in the two manuscripts marked kha and ṅa.

31.s: kiñcidrūpaṃ samāsyāya vāsudevāsya nāśaya //37//
31.d: किञ्चिद्रूपं समास्याय वासुदेवास्य नाशय //37//
31.m: assuming some form, O Vāsudeva, destroy for him! // 37

31.s:
kṣiptvā sudarśanañ cakraṃ jvālāmālātibhīṣaṇam /
sarvaduṣṭopaśamanaṃ kuru devavarācyuta //
31.d:
क्षिप्त्वा सुदर्शनञ् चक्रं ज्वालामालातिभीषणम् /
सर्वदुष्टोपशमनं कुरु देववराच्युत //
31.m:
Hurling the Sudarśana discus, exceedingly terrifying with garlands of flames,
bring about the pacification of all wicked things, O best of gods, O Acyuta!

31.s:
sudarśana mahājvāla cchindhi cchindhi mahārava(1) /
sarvaduṣṭāni rakṣāṃsi kṣayaṃ yāntu vibhīṣaṇa //
31.d:
सुदर्शन महाज्वाल च्छिन्धि च्छिन्धि महारव(1) /
सर्वदुष्टानि रक्षांसि क्षयं यान्तु विभीषण //
31.m:
O Sudarśana of great blaze, sever, sever, O loud-roaring one!
May all wicked rākṣasas meet destruction, O terrifying one!

31.s:
prācyāṃ pratīcyāṃ ca diśi dakṣiṇottaratas tathā /
rakṣāṅkarotu sarvātmā narasiṃhaḥ sugarjitaḥ(2) //
31.d:
प्राच्यां प्रतीच्यां च दिशि दक्षिणोत्तरतस् तथा /
रक्षाङ्करोतु सर्वात्मा नरसिंहः सुगर्जितः(2) //
31.m: In the east and in the west, likewise in the south and in the north, / may Narasiṃha, who has a noble roar and is the soul of all, grant protection.

31.s:
divi bhuvyantarīkṣe ca pṛṣṭhataḥ pārśvatogrataḥ /
rakṣāṅkarotu bhagavān bahurūpī janārdanaḥ //
31.d:
दिवि भुव्यन्तरीक्षे च पृष्ठतः पार्श्वतोग्रतः /
रक्षाङ्करोतु भगवान् बहुरूपी जनार्दनः //
31.m: In heaven, on earth, and in intermediate space, behind, at the sides, and in front, / may the Blessed Janārdana of many forms grant protection.

31.s:
yathā viṣṇurjagatsarvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣaṃ /
tena satyena duṣṭāni śamamasya vrajantu vai(3) //
31.d:
यथा विष्णुर्जगत्सर्वं सदेवासुरमानुषं /
तेन सत्येन दुष्टानि शममस्य व्रजन्तु वै(3) //
31.m: Just as Viṣṇu is the entire world with its gods, asuras, and humans, / by that truth, may his misfortunes indeed come to peace.

31.s:
yathā viṣṇau smṛte sadyaḥ saṅkṣayaṃ yānti pātakāḥ /
satyena tena sakalaṃ duṣṭamasya praśāmyatu //
31.d:
यथा विष्णौ स्मृते सद्यः सङ्क्षयं यान्ति पातकाः /
सत्येन तेन सकलं दुष्टमस्य प्रशाम्यतु //
31.m: Just as sins perish immediately when Viṣṇu is remembered, / by that truth, may all evil of his be pacified.

31.s:
paramātmā yathā viṣṇurvedānteṣu ca gīyate /
tena satyena sakalaṃ duṣṭamasya praśāmyatu //
31.d:
परमात्मा यथा विष्णुर्वेदान्तेषु च गीयते /
तेन सत्येन सकलं दुष्टमस्य प्रशाम्यतु //
31.m: Just as Viṣṇu is sung as the supreme Self in the Upaniṣads, / by that truth, may all evil of his be pacified.

31.s:
yathā yajñeśvaro viṣṇurdeveṣvapi hi gīyate /
satyena tena sakalaṃ yanmayoktaṃ tathāstu tat //
31.d:
यथा यज्ञेश्वरो विष्णुर्देवेष्वपि हि गीयते /
सत्येन तेन सकलं यन्मयोक्तं तथास्तु तत् //
31.m: Just as Viṣṇu is celebrated as the lord of sacrifice among the gods, / by that truth, may everything that I have spoken come to pass.

31.s:
śāntirastu śivañcāstu duṣṭamasya praśāmyatu /
vāsudevaśarīrotthaiḥ kuśair nirmathitaṃ mayā(4) //
31.d:
शान्तिरस्तु शिवञ्चास्तु दुष्टमस्य प्रशाम्यतु /
वासुदेवशरीरोत्थैः कुशैर् निर्मथितं मया(4) //
31.m: May there be peace, may there be auspiciousness, may his misfortune be pacified! / It has been stirred away by me with kuśa grass sprung from Vāsudeva's body.

31.s:
apamārjatu govindo naro nārāyaṇas tathā /
tathāstu sarvaduḥkhānāṃ praśamo japanāddhareḥ //
:n
1 mahābala iti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 svargarjitair iti ga, ṅa, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
3 prayāntu vai iti ga, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
4 kuśair nirṇāśitamiti kha, ga, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ
:p 91
31.d:
अपमार्जतु गोविन्दो नरो नारायणस् तथा /
तथास्तु सर्वदुःखानां प्रशमो जपनाद्धरेः //
:न्
1 महाबल इति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 स्वर्गर्जितैर् इति ग, ङ, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
3 प्रयान्तु वै इति ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
4 कुशैर् निर्णाशितमिति ख, ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः
:प् 91
31.m:
May Govinda, Nara, and likewise Nārāyaṇa wipe [it] away. / May all afflictions thus be pacified by recitation of Hari's name.
[Footnote]
1. "mahābala" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha.
2. "svargarjitaiḥ" is the reading in the two manuscripts marked ga and ṅa.
3. "prayāntu vai" is the reading in the manuscript marked ga.
4. "kuśair nirṇāśitam" is the reading in the two manuscripts marked kha and ga. / [Page 91]

31.s:
apamārjanakaṃ śastraṃ sarvarogādivāraṇam /
ayaṃ hariḥ kuśo viṣṇurhatā rogā mayā tava //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye kuśāpamārjanaṃ nāma ekatriṃśo
'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha dvātiṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
saṃskārakathanaṃ
31.d:
अपमार्जनकं शस्त्रं सर्वरोगादिवारणम् /
अयं हरिः कुशो विष्णुर्हता रोगा मया तव //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये कुशापमार्जनं नाम एकत्रिंशो
ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ द्वातिंशो ऽध्यायः
संस्कारकथनं
31.m:
The wiping [rite] is a weapon that wards off all diseases and ailments. / This Hari, the kuśa grass, is Viṣṇu; your diseases have been destroyed by me.
Thus in the primal Mahāpurāṇa of Agni, the thirty-first chapter, entitled "Kuśāpamārjana".
Now the thirty-second chapter:
Account of the Saṃskāras

32.s:
agnir uvāca
nirvāṇādiṣu dīkṣāsu cattvāriṃśattathāṣṭa ca /
saṃskārān kārayeddhīmān śṛṇutānyaiḥ suro bhavet //
32.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
निर्वाणादिषु दीक्षासु चत्त्वारिंशत्तथाष्ट च /
संस्कारान् कारयेद्धीमान् शृणुतान्यैः सुरो भवेत् //
32.m: Agni said: / In the liberating and other initiations, a wise man should perform forty-eight / saṃskāras. Listen to those by which one becomes a god.

32.s:
garbhādhānantu yonyāṃ vai tataḥ puṃsavanañcaret /
sīmantonnayanañcaiva jātakarma ca nāma ca //
32.d:
गर्भाधानन्तु योन्यां वै ततः पुंसवनञ्चरेत् /
सीमन्तोन्नयनञ्चैव जातकर्म च नाम च //
32.m: One should perform the conception rite in the womb, then the puṃsavana rite, / the parting of the hair, the birth rite, and the naming rite,

32.s:
annāśanaṃ tataścūḍā brahmacaryavratāni ca /
catvāri vaiṣṇavī pārthī bhautikī śrotrikī tathā //
32.d:
अन्नाशनं ततश्चूडा ब्रह्मचर्यव्रतानि च /
चत्वारि वैष्णवी पार्थी भौतिकी श्रोत्रिकी तथा //
32.m: first feeding of food, then tonsure, and the four observances of studentship: / Vaiṣṇavī, Pārthī, Bhautikī, and Śrotrikī,

32.s:
godānaṃ sūtakatvañca pākayajñāś ca sapta te(1) /
aṣṭakā pārvaṇaśrāddhaṃ śrāvaṇyagrāyaṇīti ca //
32.d:
गोदानं सूतकत्वञ्च पाकयज्ञाश् च सप्त ते(1) /
अष्टका पार्वणश्राद्धं श्रावण्यग्रायणीति च //
32.m: the gift of a cow, and the end of birth-impurity; and these are the seven cooked sacrifices: / the aṣṭakā, the pārvaṇaśrāddha, the śrāvaṇī, the āgrayaṇī,

32.s:
caitrī cāśvayujī sapta haviryajñāṃś ca tān śṛṇu /
ādhānañcāgnihotrañca darśo vai paurṇamāsakaḥ //
32.d:
चैत्री चाश्वयुजी सप्त हविर्यज्ञांश् च तान् शृणु /
आधानञ्चाग्निहोत्रञ्च दर्शो वै पौर्णमासकः //
32.m: the caitrī, and the āśvayujī. And listen to those seven oblation sacrifices: / the establishment of the sacred fire, the agnihotra, the new moon sacrifice, the full moon sacrifice,

32.s:
cāturmāsyaṃ paśubandhaḥ sautrāmaṇirathāparaḥ /
somasaṃsthāḥ sapta śṛṇu agniṣṭomaḥ kratūttamaḥ //
32.d:
चातुर्मास्यं पशुबन्धः सौत्रामणिरथापरः /
सोमसंस्थाः सप्त शृणु अग्निष्टोमः क्रतूत्तमः //
32.m: the cāturmāsya, the animal sacrifice, and then another, the sautrāmaṇī. / Hear the seven forms of the soma sacrifice: the agniṣṭoma, the best of sacrifices,

32.s:
atyagniṣṭoma ukthaś ca ṣoḍaśo vājapeyakaḥ /
atirātrāptoryāmaś ca sahasreśāḥ savā ime //
32.d:
अत्यग्निष्टोम उक्थश् च षोडशो वाजपेयकः /
अतिरात्राप्तोर्यामश् च सहस्रेशाः सवा इमे //
32.m: the atyagniṣṭoma, the ukthya, the ṣoḍaśin, the vājapeya, / the atirātra, and the āptoryāma. These are the savas, lords of thousands:

32.s:
hiraṇyāṅghrirhiraṇyākṣo hiraṇyamitra ity ataḥ /
:n
1 sapta ca iti ga, kha, cihnitapustkadvayapāṭhaḥ
:p 92
hiraṇyapāṇirhemākṣo hemāṅgo hemasūtrakaḥ //
32.d:
हिरण्याङ्घ्रिर्हिरण्याक्षो हिरण्यमित्र इत्य् अतः /
:न्
1 सप्त च इति ग, ख, चिह्नितपुस्त्कद्वयपाठः
:प् 92
हिरण्यपाणिर्हेमाक्षो हेमाङ्गो हेमसूत्रकः //
32.m:
the hiraṇyāṅghri, the hiraṇyākṣa, and therefore the hiraṇyamitra,
[Footnote]
1. "sapta ca" is the reading in the two manuscripts marked ga and kha. / [Page 92]
the hiraṇyapāṇi, the hemākṣa, the hemāṅga, the hemasūtraka,

32.s:
hiraṇyāsyo hiraṇyāṅgo hemajihvo hiraṇyavān /
aśvamedho hi sarveśo guṇāścāṣṭātha tān śṛṇu //
32.d:
हिरण्यास्यो हिरण्याङ्गो हेमजिह्वो हिरण्यवान् /
अश्वमेधो हि सर्वेशो गुणाश्चाष्टाथ तान् शृणु //
32.m: the hiraṇyāsya, the hiraṇyāṅga, the hemajihva, and the hiraṇyavat; / indeed, the horse sacrifice is the lord of all. Now hear those eight virtues:

32.s:
dayā ca sarvabhūteṣu kṣāntiś caiva tathārjavam /
śaucaṃ caivamanāyāso maṅgalaṃ cāparo guṇaḥ //
32.d:
दया च सर्वभूतेषु क्षान्तिश् चैव तथार्जवम् /
शौचं चैवमनायासो मङ्गलं चापरो गुणः //
32.m: compassion toward all beings, patience, uprightness, / purity, freedom from anxiety, and another virtue is auspiciousness,

32.s:
akārpaṇyañcāspṛhā ca mūlena juhuyācchatam /
sauraśākteyaviṣṇvīśadīkṣāstvete samāḥ smṛtāḥ //
32.d:
अकार्पण्यञ्चास्पृहा च मूलेन जुहुयाच्छतम् /
सौरशाक्तेयविष्ण्वीशदीक्षास्त्वेते समाः स्मृताः //
32.m: absence of stinginess, and desirelessness. One should make one hundred oblations with the root mantra. / These initiations of Sūrya, Śakti, Viṣṇu, and Śiva are considered equal.

32.s:
saṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛtaś caitair bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt /
sarvarogādvinirmukto devavadvartate naraḥ /
japyāddhomātpūjanācca dhyānāddevasya ceṣṭabhāk //
:e ity ādimahāpurāṇe āgneye aṣṭacatvāriṃśatsaṃskārakathanaṃ
nāma dvātriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha trayastriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
pavitrārohaṇavidhānaṃ
32.d:
संस्कारैः संस्कृतश् चैतैर् भुक्तिमुक्तिमवाप्नुयात् /
सर्वरोगाद्विनिर्मुक्तो देववद्वर्तते नरः /
जप्याद्धोमात्पूजनाच्च ध्यानाद्देवस्य चेष्टभाक् //
:ए इत्य् आदिमहापुराणे आग्नेये अष्टचत्वारिंशत्संस्कारकथनं
नाम द्वात्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ त्रयस्त्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
पवित्रारोहणविधानं
32.m:
Consecrated by these saṃskāras, one obtains worldly enjoyment and liberation; / freed from all disease, a man lives like a god; / through recitation, fire oblation, worship, and meditation on the deity, he attains his desires.
Thus in the primal Mahāpurāṇa of Agni, the thirty-second chapter, entitled "Account of the Forty-Eight Saṃskāras".
Now the thirty-third chapter:
Rule for the Investiture with the Sacred Thread

33.s:
agnir uvāca
pavitrārohaṇaṃ vakṣye varṣapūjākalaṃ hareḥ /
āṣāḍhādau kārtikānte pratipadvanadā tithiḥ(1) //
33.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
पवित्रारोहणं वक्ष्ये वर्षपूजाकलं हरेः /
आषाढादौ कार्तिकान्ते प्रतिपद्वनदा तिथिः(1) //
33.m: Agni said: / I will explain the investiture with the sacred thread, yielding the fruit of a year's worship of Hari. / From Āṣāḍha onwards to the end of Kārtika, the lunar days bestow wealth:

33.s:
śriyā gauryā gaṇeśasya sarasvatyā guhasya ca /
mārtaṇḍamātṛdurgāṇāṃ nāgarṣiharimanmathaiḥ //
33.d:
श्रिया गौर्या गणेशस्य सरस्वत्या गुहस्य च /
मार्तण्डमातृदुर्गाणां नागर्षिहरिमन्मथैः //
33.m: for Śrī, Gaurī, Gaṇeśa, Sarasvatī, and Guha, / for the Sun, the Mothers, the Durgās, the serpent deities, the sages, Hari, and Manmatha,

33.s:
śivasya brahmaṇastadvaddvitīyādititheḥ kramāt /
yasya devasya yo bhaktaḥ pavitrā tasya sā tithiḥ //
33.d:
शिवस्य ब्रह्मणस्तद्वद्द्वितीयादितिथेः क्रमात् /
यस्य देवस्य यो भक्तः पवित्रा तस्य सा तिथिः //
33.m: likewise for Śiva and Brahmā, in the order of lunar days beginning with the second lunar day. / The sacred thread belongs to whatever deity one is devoted to, on that lunar day.

33.s:
ārohaṇe tulyavidhiḥ pṛthak mantrādikaṃ yadi /
:n
1 vardhate tithiriti kha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 93
sauvarṇe rājataṃ tāmraṃ netrakārpāsikādikaṃ //
33.d:
आरोहणे तुल्यविधिः पृथक् मन्त्रादिकं यदि /
:न्
1 वर्धते तिथिरिति ख, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 93
सौवर्णे राजतं ताम्रं नेत्रकार्पासिकादिकं //
33.m:
The ritual is identical in the investiture, even if mantras and the like are separate.
[Footnote]
1. "vardhate tithiḥ" is the reading in the manuscript marked kha. / [Page 93]
[It may be made] of gold, silver, copper, silk, cotton, and the like.

33.s:
brāhmaṇyā kartitaṃ sūtraṃ tadalābhe tu saṃskṛtaṃ /
triguṇaṃ triguṇīkṛtya tena kuryāt pavitrakaṃ //
33.d:
ब्राह्मण्या कर्तितं सूत्रं तदलाभे तु संस्कृतं /
त्रिगुणं त्रिगुणीकृत्य तेन कुर्यात् पवित्रकं //
33.m: Thread spun by a Brahmin woman, or consecrated if that is unavailable, / having tripled it and tripled it again, one should make the sacred thread with it.

33.s:
aṣtottaraśatādūrdhvaṃ tadardhaṃ cottamādikaṃ /
kriyālopāvighātārthaṃ yattvayābhihitaṃ prabho //
33.d:
अष्तोत्तरशतादूर्ध्वं तदर्धं चोत्तमादिकं /
क्रियालोपाविघातार्थं यत्त्वयाभिहितं प्रभो //
33.m: Above one hundred and eight [threads], and half that, are the best and middle kinds. / "O Lord, for the purpose of removing impediments from defects in the rite, that which was declared by You,

33.s:
mayā tat kriyate deva yathā yatra pāvitrakaṃ /
avighnaṃ tu bhavedatra kuru nātha jayāvyaya //
33.d:
मया तत् क्रियते देव यथा यत्र पावित्रकं /
अविघ्नं तु भवेदत्र कुरु नाथ जयाव्यय //
33.m: that is being performed by me, O God, as and where the sacred thread [is offered]. / Let there be no obstacle here; make it so, O victorious and imperishable Master!"

33.s:
prārthya tanmaṇḍalāyādau gāyatryā bandhayennaraḥ /
oṃ nārāyaṇāya vidmahe vāsudevāya dhīmahi //
33.d:
प्रार्थ्य तन्मण्डलायादौ गायत्र्या बन्धयेन्नरः /
ओं नारायणाय विद्महे वासुदेवाय धीमहि //
33.m: Having prayed thus to the maṇḍala at first, a man should tie it with the Gāyatrī: / "Om, we know Nārāyaṇa; we meditate on Vāsudeva;

33.s:
tanno viṣṇuḥ pracodayāt devadevānurūpataḥ /
jānūrunābhināmāntaṃ pratimāsu pavitrakaṃ //
33.d:
तन्नो विष्णुः प्रचोदयात् देवदेवानुरूपतः /
जानूरुनाभिनामान्तं प्रतिमासु पवित्रकं //
33.m: may that Viṣṇu impel us." According to the deity of deities, / the sacred thread on images should reach to the knees, thighs, or navel.

33.s:
pādāntā vanamālā syādaṣṭottrasahasrataḥ(1) /
mālā tu kalpasādhyaṃ vā dviguṇaṃ ṣoḍaśāṅgulāt //
33.d:
पादान्ता वनमाला स्यादष्टोत्त्रसहस्रतः(1) /
माला तु कल्पसाध्यं वा द्विगुणं षोडशाङ्गुलात् //
33.m: Reaching to the feet, it is a forest garland, made of a thousand and eight [threads]; / or the garland may be made according to ritual rule, double that of sixteen finger-breadths.

33.s:
karṇikā keśaraṃ patraṃ mantrādyaṃ(2) maṇḍalāntakaṃ /
maṇḍalāṅgulamātraikacakrābjādyau(3) pavitrakaṃ //
33.d:
कर्णिका केशरं पत्रं मन्त्राद्यं(2) मण्डलान्तकं /
मण्डलाङ्गुलमात्रैकचक्राब्जाद्यौ(3) पवित्रकं //
33.m: From the pericarp, filaments, petals, beginning with mantras, up to the end of the maṇḍala; / the sacred thread for the discus, lotus, and others is merely the finger-breadths of the maṇḍala.

33.s:
sthaṇḍile 'ṅgulamānena ātmanaḥ saptaviṃśatiḥ /
ācāryāṇāṃ ca sūtrāṇi pitṛmātrādipustake //
33.d:
स्थण्डिले ऽङ्गुलमानेन आत्मनः सप्तविंशतिः /
आचार्याणां च सूत्राणि पितृमात्रादिपुस्तके //
33.m: On an altar, by measure of finger-breadths, twenty-seven for oneself; / and the threads for teachers, on books of parents and others,

33.s:
nābhyantaṃ dvādaśagranthiṃ tathā gandhapavitrake /
dvyaṅgulāt kalpanādau dvirmālā cāṣṭottaraṃ śataṃ //
33.d:
नाभ्यन्तं द्वादशग्रन्थिं तथा गन्धपवित्रके /
द्व्यङ्गुलात् कल्पनादौ द्विर्माला चाष्टोत्तरं शतं //
33.m: reaching to the navel, with twelve knots, likewise in the fragrant sacred thread. / In making it two finger-breadths from the beginning, the double garland has one hundred and eight [knots],

33.s:
athavārkacaturviṃśaṣaḍtriṃśanmālikā dvijaḥ /
anāmāmadhyamāṅguṣṭhair mandādyaiḥ mālikārthibhiḥ (4) //
:n
1 pādāntareṇa mālā syādaṣṭottarasahasraśaḥ iti ga,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
2 gadādyamiti gha, cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
3 cakrāṅgadau pavitrake iti gha, cihnitaputakapāṭhaḥ
4 mandādau iti kha, ga, cihnitapustakadvayapāṭhaḥ mandrādyair iti gha,
cihnitapustakapāṭhaḥ
:p 94
33.d:
अथवार्कचतुर्विंशषड्त्रिंशन्मालिका द्विजः /
अनामामध्यमाङ्गुष्ठैर् मन्दाद्यैः मालिकार्थिभिः (4) //
:न्
1 पादान्तरेण माला स्यादष्टोत्तरसहस्रशः इति ग,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
2 गदाद्यमिति घ, चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
3 चक्राङ्गदौ पवित्रके इति घ, चिह्नितपुतकपाठः
4 मन्दादौ इति ख, ग, चिह्नितपुस्तकद्वयपाठः मन्द्राद्यैर् इति घ,
चिह्नितपुस्तकपाठः
:प् 94
33.m:
or a twice-born person may make a garland of twelve, twenty-four, or thirty-six [knots], / using the ring finger, middle finger, and thumb, by those seeking garlands from slow [recitation] and so on.

33.s:
kaniṣṭādau dvādaśa vā granthayaḥ syuḥ pavitrake /
raveḥ kumbhahutāśādeḥ sambhave viṣṇuvanmatam //
33.d:
कनिष्टादौ द्वादश वा ग्रन्थयः स्युः पवित्रके /
रवेः कुम्भहुताशादेः सम्भवे विष्णुवन्मतम् //
33.m: Or there may be twelve knots in the sacred thread, beginning from the little finger. / In the presence of the Sun, the water-pot, the fire, and so forth, the view is that it is like that of Viṣṇu.

33.s:
pīṭhasya pīṭhamānaṃ syānmekhalānte ca kuṇḍakaṃ /
yathāśakti sūtragranthiparicāretha vaiṣṇave //
33.d:
पीठस्य पीठमानं स्यान्मेखलान्ते च कुण्डकं /
यथाशक्ति सूत्रग्रन्थिपरिचारेथ वैष्णवे //
33.m: The size of the pedestal should be the measure of the altar, and a small pit at the end of the belt, / according to capacity, in the attendant service of the cord-knots in the Vaiṣṇava rite.

33.s:
sūtrāṇi vā saptadaśa sūtreṇa trivibhaktake(1) /
rocanāgurukarpūraharidrākuṅkumādibhiḥ //
33.d:
सूत्राणि वा सप्तदश सूत्रेण त्रिविभक्तके(1) /
रोचनागुरुकर्पूरहरिद्राकुङ्कुमादिभिः //
33.m: Or seventeen threads, divided threefold by a thread; / with rocanā, agallochum, camphor, turmeric, saffron, and so forth,

33.s:
rañjayeccandanādyair vā snānasandhyādikṛnnaraḥ /
ekādaśyāṃ yāgagṛhe bhagavantaṃ hariṃ jayet //
33.d:
रञ्जयेच्चन्दनाद्यैर् वा स्नानसन्ध्यादिकृन्नरः /
एकादश्यां यागगृहे भगवन्तं हरिं जयेत् //
33.m: or with sandal paste and the like, a man, having performed his bath, twilight prayers, and other rites, should dye [them]. / On the eleventh lunar day, in the sacrificial hall, he should worship the Lord Hari.

33.s:
samastaparivārāya baliṃ pīṭhe samarcayet /
kṣyauṃ kṣetrapālāya dvārānte dvāropari tathā śriyaṃ //
33.d:
समस्तपरिवाराय बलिं पीठे समर्चयेत् /
क्ष्यौं क्षेत्रपालाय द्वारान्ते द्वारोपरि तथा श्रियं //
33.m: He should offer bali on the pedestal to the entire retinue: / with "Kṣyauṃ to Kṣetrapāla" at the door, and above the door to Śrī likewise;

33.s:
dhātre dakṣe vidhātre ca gaṅgāñca yamunāṃ tathā /
śaṅkhapadmanidhī pūjya madhye vāstvapasāraṇaṃ //
sāraṅgāyeti bhūtānāṃ bhūtaśuddhiṃ sthitaś caret //

33.m:
to Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ on the right, and to Gaṅgā and Yamunā likewise. / Having worshipped the treasures Śaṅkha and Padma, the removal of the spirits of the site in the center / with "To Sāraṅga", standing, he should perform the purification of elements of the living beings.
"Oṃ hrūṃ haḥ phaṭ hrūṃ, I dissolve the subtle element of smell, homage!"
"Oṃ hrūṃ haḥ phaṭ hrūṃ, I dissolve the subtle element of taste, homage! / Oṃ hrūṃ haḥ phaṭ hrūṃ, I dissolve the subtle element of form, homage!"
"Oṃ hrūṃ haḥ phaṭ hrūṃ, I dissolve the subtle element of touch, homage!"
[Footnotes]
1 "And three threads in the bhadraka", reads manuscript marked gha.
2 "oṃ hūṃ haḥ phaṭ hūm", reads manuscript marked ga; "oṃ hrāṃ haḥ phaṭ hrūm", reads manuscript marked ṅa.
2 "oṃ hrīṃ haḥ phaṭ hrūn", reads manuscript marked ṅa.

33.s:
pañcodghātair gandhatanmātrarūpaṃ bhūmimaṇḍalaṃ /
caturasrañca pītañca kaṭhinaṃ vajralāñchitam //
33.d:
पञ्चोद्घातैर् गन्धतन्मात्ररूपं भूमिमण्डलं /
चतुरस्रञ्च पीतञ्च कठिनं वज्रलाञ्छितम् //
33.m: With five breath-expulsions, the circle of earth consisting of the subtle element of smell, / square, yellow, firm, marked with a vajra,

33.s:
indrādhidaivataṃ pādayugmamadhyagataṃ smaret /
śuddhañca rasatanmātraṃ pravilipyātha saṃharet //
rasamātrarūpamātre krameṇānena pūjakaḥ //

namaḥ

शुद्धञ्च रसतन्मात्रं प्रविलिप्याथ संहरेत् //
रसमात्ररूपमात्रे क्रमेणानेन पूजकः //

नमः

नमः
33.m:
presided over by Indra, located between the pair of feet, he should visualize; / and having anointed the pure subtle element of taste, he should then dissolve it. / In the mere form of the subtle element of taste, by this order the worshipper [should dissolve]:
"Oṃ hrīṃ haḥ phaṭ hrūṃ, I dissolve the subtle element of taste, homage!"
"Oṃ hrūṃ haḥ phaṭ, I dissolve the subtle element of form, homage!"
"Oṃ hrīṃ haḥ phaṭ hrūṃ, I dissolve the subtle element of touch, homage!"
"Oṃ hrīṃ haḥ phaṭ hrūṃ, I dissolve the subtle element of sound, homage!"

33.s:
jānunābhimadhyagataṃ(5) śvetaṃ vai padmalāñchitaṃ /
śuklavarṇaṃ cārdhacandraṃ dhyāyedvaruṇadaivataṃ //
33.d:
जानुनाभिमध्यगतं(5) श्वेतं वै पद्मलाञ्छितं /
शुक्लवर्णं चार्धचन्द्रं ध्यायेद्वरुणदैवतं //
33.m: Located between the knees and navel, white, marked with a lotus, / of white color, and a half-moon, presided over by Varuṇa, he should meditate upon;

33.s:
caturbhiś ca tadudghātaiḥ śuddhaṃ tadrasamātrakaṃ /
saṃharedrūpatanmātrai rūpamātre ca saṃharet //

namaḥ

namaḥ

चतुर्भिश् च तदुद्घातैः शुद्धं तद्रसमात्रकं /
संहरेद्रूपतन्मात्रै रूपमात्रे च संहरेत् //

नमः

नमः

नमः
33.m:
and with four breath-expulsions of it, that pure subtle element of taste / he should dissolve into the subtle elements of form, and dissolve into the subtle element of form:
"Oṃ hrūṃ haḥ phaṭ hrūṃ, I dissolve the subtle element of form, homage!"
"Oṃ hrūṃ haḥ phaṭ hrūṃ, I dissolve the subtle element of touch, homage!"
"Oṃ hrūṃ haḥ phaṭ hrūṃ, I dissolve the subtle element of sound, homage!"

33.s:
iti tribhistadudghātaistrikoṇaṃ vahnimaṇḍalam /
nābhikaṇṭhamadhyagataṃ raktaṃ svastikalāñchitaṃ //
33.d:
इति त्रिभिस्तदुद्घातैस्त्रिकोणं वह्निमण्डलम् /
नाभिकण्ठमध्यगतं रक्तं स्वस्तिकलाञ्छितं //
33.m: Thus, with three breath-expulsions of it, the triangular circle of fire, / located between the navel and the throat, red, marked with a svastika,

33.s:
dhyātvānalādhidaivantacchuddhaṃ sparśe layaṃ nayat /

kaṇṭhanāsāmadhyagataṃ vṛttaṃ vai vāyumaṇḍalam //

कण्ठनासामध्यगतं वृत्तं वै वायुमण्डलम् //
33.m:
having meditated upon it presided over by Fire, he should lead that pure [element] to dissolution in touch.

1 "oṃ hrāṃ haḥ phaṭ ham", reads manuscript marked ga.
2 "oṃ hrīṃ phaṭ ham", reads manuscript marked ga; "oṃ hrūṃ haḥ phaṭ hūm", reads manuscript marked ṅa.

4 "oṃ hraṃ haḥ phaṭ hūm", reads manuscript marked ṅa.
